The image features the mold’s gelatinous fruiting bodies, which release spores as part of reproduction. To bring the delicate structures into sharp detail, Eric Epstein stacked 240 images.
paras.zh: 这种粘菌（Hemitrichia sp.）是在纽约布鲁克林市中心发现的，它是从展望公园的一根腐烂的木头上发芽的。该图像展示了霉菌的凝胶状子实体，其释放孢子作为繁殖的一部分。为了将精致的结构呈现为清晰的细节，Eric Epstein 堆叠了 240 张图像。

paras.en: First, Epstein searched local parks for slime molds to photograph, carefully cutting pieces of waterlogged wood free without disturbing his subjects. “In this liquidy state, any touch would demolish” the fruiting bodies, he says.
paras.zh: 首先，爱泼斯坦在当地公园寻找粘菌进行拍摄，小心翼翼地切掉浸水的木头，而不打扰他的拍摄对象。 “在这种液体状态下，任何触摸都会破坏”子实体，他说。

paras.en: One species of slime mold closely mirrors the cosmic web of gas and dark matter connecting galaxies, which helps scientists to more accurately map the cosmos. Another species has fascinated researchers for its ability to pack a store of bacteria to feed the next generation, when it’s near death.
paras.zh: 一种粘菌密切地反映了连接星系的气体和暗物质的宇宙网络，这有助于科学家更准确地绘制宇宙图。另一种物种令研究人员着迷，因为它能够在下一代濒临死亡时储存大量细菌来喂养下一代。

paras.en: Epstein hopes the photograph hints “at [a] vast array of activity beyond our unaided perception.” The image won sixth place in the competition.
paras.zh: 爱泼斯坦希望这张照片暗示“一系列超出我们肉眼感知的活动”。该图像在比赛中获得了第六名。

paras.en: This cell could have become anything in the body. Through some scientific nudging, it burst into a brilliant neuron.
paras.zh: 这个细胞可以变成体内的任何东西。经过一些科学的推动，它突然变成了一个聪明的神经元。

paras.en: Clusters of nuclei, looking like flashpoints in an intricate web, were captured by undergraduate student Faith Fernandes and structural cell biologist James Glover at the University of California, Berkeley.
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校的本科生 Faith Fernandes 和结构细胞生物学家 James Glover 捕捉到了看起来像错综复杂的网络中的闪点的细胞核簇。

paras.en: The image commemorates the team’s first attempt at crafting neurons from a particular kind of stem cell. “I was so instantly enamored with this piece that I made it my computer wallpaper as soon as it was taken,” Fernandes says.
paras.zh: 该图像是为了纪念该团队首次尝试从特定类型的干细胞中制造神经元。 “我立刻就被这幅作品迷住了，拍完后我就把它作为我的电脑壁纸，”费尔南德斯说。

paras.en: The eruption of color depicts human induced pluripotent stem cells, which can become any type of cell in the body, that have developed into neurons. The neurotubules, which contribute to the structure of and transportation of intracellular molecules, appear blue. Orange indicates where the DNA is located.
paras.zh: 颜色的爆发描绘了人类诱导的多能干细胞，它可以成为体内任何类型的细胞，并发育成神经元。有助于细胞内分子的结构和运输的神经管呈蓝色。橙色表示 DNA 所在的位置。

paras.en: The stem cells are created by reprogramming adult cells to a stage before the cell was locked into a path to become a specific type of cell. They are studied for their many potential applications in regenerative medicine.
paras.zh: 干细胞是通过将成体细胞重新编程到细胞被锁定成为特定类型细胞的路径之前的阶段而产生的。人们对它们在再生医学中的许多潜在应用进行了研究。

paras.en: Fernandes says she hopes that studying these cells will illuminate ways to address neurodegeneration in diseases such as Parkinson’s disease. Already, researchers have used these cells to regrow eye tissue, address premature aging in mouse studies and grow organs. The shot won an Image of Distinction title in the competition.
paras.zh: 费尔南德斯说，她希望研究这些细胞能够阐明解决帕金森病等疾病中神经退行性疾病的方法。研究人员已经利用这些细胞来再生眼组织、解决小鼠研究中的过早衰老问题以及培育器官。该镜头在比赛中获得了“杰出形象”称号。

articles.title: A lifesaving medication is not behind the drop in U.S. overdose deaths
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: Drug overdose deaths unexpectedly took a nosedive in the United States a few years ago. But it doesn’t appear to be due to more people being revived than before.
paras.zh: 几年前，美国吸毒过量死亡人数出人意料地大幅下降。但这似乎并不是因为复活的人比以前更多。

paras.en: At the peak in mid-2023, there were around 111,000 drug overdose deaths per year in the United States. By the end of 2025, the number had fallen to under 71,000 per year, and researchers are still piecing together why. One theory: The wider availability of naloxone, a medication that reverses opioid overdoses, made it possible to revive more people than before.
paras.zh: 在 2023 年中期的高峰期，美国每年约有 111,000 人因药物过量死亡。到 2025 年底，这一数字已降至每年 71,000 人以下，研究人员仍在拼凑原因。一种理论是：纳洛酮（一种逆转阿片类药物过量的药物）的广泛使用使得比以前更多的人得以复活。

paras.en: But a study of U.S. emergency medical services agencies found that emergency medical responses for nonfatal overdoses dropped along with deaths, and the use of naloxone also declined. That suggests that fewer overdoses overall occurred, not that naloxone stopped deaths more often, researchers report October 21 in the Journal of the American Medical Association.
paras.zh: 但对美国紧急医疗服务机构的一项研究发现，对非致命性用药过量的紧急医疗反应随着死亡人数的减少而下降，纳洛酮的使用也有所下降。研究人员 10 月 21 日在《美国医学会杂志》上报告称，这表明总体上服用过量的情况较少，而不是纳洛酮更频繁地阻止了死亡。

paras.en: “Naloxone still saves lives every day,” says Michael Barnett, a health services researcher at Brown University School of Public Health in Providence, R.I. “But it doesn’t look like the reason for the sudden turn” in overdose deaths.
paras.zh: 罗得岛州普罗维登斯布朗大学公共卫生学院的卫生服务研究员迈克尔·巴尼特说：“纳洛酮仍然每天都在拯救生命，但它看起来不像是过量死亡突然转变的原因”。

paras.en: State policies, community distribution programs and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration’s approval of the nasal spray version of naloxone as an over-the counter drug have expanded access.
paras.zh: 国家政策、社区分配计划以及美国食品和药物管理局批准鼻喷雾剂纳洛酮作为非处方药扩大了使用范围。

paras.en: Barnett and colleagues analyzed nearly 186 million emergency medical service activations — an ambulance or other EMS response after a 911 call — nationwide that occurred from May 2020 through December 2025. Of 2.5 million responses for nonfatal drug overdoses, 40.5 percent involved opioids.
paras.zh: Barnett 及其同事分析了 2020 年 5 月至 2025 年 12 月期间全国范围内发生的近 1.86 亿次紧急医疗服务启动（即接到 911 电话后救护车或其他 EMS 响应）。在 250 万次非致命药物过量响应中，40.5% 涉及阿片类药物。

paras.en: From May of 2023 onward, EMS activations for nonfatal opioid overdoses fell on average by about 6,000, or around 33 percent, below what was expected. Total administrations of naloxone dropped as well, by around 4,700 on average, or 21 percent below what was expected. The study suggests that naloxone was not used more often than before by bystanders prior to the EMS response, but did not include data on cases when a bystander provided naloxone and no one called 911.
paras.zh: 从 2023 年 5 月起，非致命阿片类药物过量的 EMS 激活平均下降约 6,000 例，即约 33%，低于预期。纳洛酮的给药总数也有所下降，平均减少约 4,700 次，比预期低 21%。该研究表明，在 EMS 响应之前，旁观者使用纳洛酮的频率并不比以前更高，但不包括旁观者提供纳洛酮且无人拨打 911 的情况的数据。

paras.en: Additional possibilities to explain the steep drop in overdose deaths — which followed a three-decade increase — include changes to the illicit opioid supply or with the population of people at risk for overdoses. “My own read is that a disruption in the fentanyl supply best explains how sudden and widespread the turn was,” Barnett says. “Underneath it, the population at risk has probably been shrinking for years.”
paras.zh: 解释服药过量死亡人数在过去三个十年增加之后急剧下降的其他可能性包括非法阿片类药物供应的变化或面临服药过量风险的人口数量。 “我自己的解读是，芬太尼供应的中断最能解释这种转变的突然性和广泛性，”巴尼特说。 “在其之下，面临风险的人口多年来可能一直在减少。”

paras.en: But “a supply-driven decline can reverse,” Barnett says, noting that the decline in overdose deaths slowed in 2025. Traffickers can adapt “by finding new chemical sources or turning to more potent synthetic opioids.”
paras.zh: 但巴尼特表示，“供应驱动的下降可能会逆转”，并指出 2025 年用药过量死亡人数的下降速度会放缓。贩运者可以“通过寻找新的化学来源或转向更有效的合成阿片类药物”来适应。

articles.title: Why did humans’ brains surpass chimps’? A tiny foe might help explain it
articles.author: Jake Buehler

paras.en: Viruses may be minuscule, but one could have influenced major differences between human and chimpanzee brains.
paras.zh: 病毒可能很小，但一种病毒可能影响人类和黑猩猩大脑之间的重大差异。

paras.en: Millions of years ago, a virus left DNA behind in an African ape’s genome, and the genetic material stuck around in modern day chimps. Those ghosts of infections past appear to influence genes involved in neuron development, which may help explain how human and chimp brains ended up so different, researchers report October 23 in Science Advances.
paras.zh: 数百万年前，一种病毒在非洲猿的基因组中留下了 DNA，而这些遗传物质则留在了现代黑猩猩的体内。研究人员在 10 月 23 日的《科学进展》杂志上报告称，过去的感染痕迹似乎会影响与神经元发育有关的基因，这可能有助于解释人类和黑猩猩的大脑为何会如此不同。

paras.en: Compared with the brains of their chimpanzee kin, human brains are three times larger and more cognitively powerful. Yet “most of their protein-making genes are very similar,” says Johan Jakobsson, a neuroscientist at Lund University in Sweden. In the absence of large differences in the genetic code, Jakobsson and his colleagues decided to look at the parts of the human and chimp genome that control when and where genes are turned on or off.
paras.zh: 与黑猩猩近亲的大脑相比，人类的大脑大三倍，认知能力也更强。然而，“它们的大多数蛋白质制造基因都非常相似，”瑞典隆德大学的神经科学家约翰·雅各布森说。在遗传密码不存在巨大差异的情况下，雅各布森和他的同事决定研究人类和黑猩猩基因组中控制基因开启或关闭的时间和地点的部分。

paras.en: Changes in gene regulation can come from viruses. Some viruses called retroviruses insert their own DNA into their hosts’ genomes to command host cells to build more viruses. But those parasitic bits of DNA can linger long after an infection. If this happens in reproductive cells, the viral DNA gets passed down with the host’s DNA.
paras.zh: 基因调控的变化可能来自病毒。一些称为逆转录病毒的病毒将自己的 DNA 插入宿主的基因组中，以命令宿主细胞构建更多病毒。但这些寄生 DNA 片段在感染后仍会残留很长时间。如果这种情况发生在生殖细胞中，病毒 DNA 就会与宿主的 DNA 一起传递下去。

paras.en: These leftover bits, called endogenous retroviruses, no longer code for the production of infectious viruses, but they can have a big impact on the host’s biology — especially if they make copies of themselves across the genome. And they have. Such viral remnants make up at least 8 percent of the genomes of humans and chimps alike. More generally, these DNA leftovers have been linked with some major evolutionary events, such as the evolution of the mammalian placenta.
paras.zh: 这些残留的片段被称为内源性逆转录病毒，不再编码感染性病毒的产生，但它们可以对宿主的生物学产生重大影响——特别是如果它们在整个基因组中复制自身的话。他们确实做到了。这些病毒残留物至少占人类和黑猩猩基因组的 8%。更一般地说，这些 DNA 残留物与一些重大进化事件有关，例如哺乳动物胎盘的进化。

paras.en: Jakobsson and his colleagues focused on a particular viral vestige in chimps. The holdover came from an infection in an ancestral African ape somewhere between 5 million and 7 million years ago. In chimpanzees, the viral DNA had stuck itself into the genome at 158 different locations. However, it is curiously absent in humans. It’s still unknown why.
paras.zh: 雅各布森和他的同事们专注于黑猩猩身上的一种特殊病毒痕迹。这种残留来自 500 万至 700 万年前非洲猿猴祖先的感染。在黑猩猩中，病毒 DNA 已嵌入基因组的 158 个不同位置。然而，奇怪的是，它在人类中却缺失。目前尚不清楚原因。

paras.en: The researchers wanted to know how that exact pathogen footprint might affect chimpanzees’ brains compared with those of humans. Working with chimpanzee stem cells, they removed the viral DNA using CRISPR, a gene editing technology that allows for precise, targeted cuts in DNA. Once the viral DNA was gone, a nearby gene called LINC00662 — normally silenced in chimpanzees — turned on, making RNA the team could detect. This matches the normal condition in human brain cells, in which LINC00662 is active. The team also used CRISPR to shut off LINC00662 in the human cells, matching the silenced condition seen in chimpanzees.
paras.zh: 研究人员想知道与人类相比，病原体的确切足迹如何影响黑猩猩的大脑。他们利用黑猩猩干细胞，利用 CRISPR 去除了病毒 DNA，这是一种基因编辑技术，可以对 DNA 进行精确、有针对性的切割。一旦病毒 DNA 消失，附近一个名为 LINC00662 的基因（在黑猩猩中通常处于沉默状态）就会开启，产生团队可以检测到的 RNA。这与 LINC00662 处于活跃状态的人脑细胞的正常状态相符。研究小组还使用 CRISPR 关闭人类细胞中的 LINC00662，与黑猩猩中观察到的沉默状态相匹配。

paras.en: When LINC00662 was active in chimp or human cells, the researchers noticed activity boosts to other genes that may be important to brain development — such as genes involved in the development and maturation of neurons and in making new neural connections. It’s not yet clear exactly how the viral DNA’s shutdown of this brain gene network affected the biology of chimpanzee brains. However, this genetic difference may have contributed to a divergence in how human and chimpanzee brains evolved, Jakobsson says. “Our findings show one way an ancient viral [DNA] insertion could create a lasting difference in how a gene is regulated in humans and chimpanzees,” Jakobsson says. Other genetic and environmental changes could be involved in the puzzle as well, he says.
paras.zh: 当 LINC00662 在黑猩猩或人类细胞中活跃时，研究人员注意到其他可能对大脑发育很重要的基因的活性增强，例如参与神经元发育和成熟以及建立新神经连接的基因。目前尚不清楚病毒 DNA 关闭大脑基因网络是如何影响黑猩猩大脑的生物学的。然而，雅各布森说，这种遗传差异可能导致了人类和黑猩猩大脑进化方式的差异。 “我们的研究结果表明，古代病毒 [DNA] 插入可以对人类和黑猩猩的基因调控方式产生持久的差异，”Jakobsson 说。他说，其他遗传和环境变化也可能与这个难题有关。

paras.en: Researchers have previously looked to single letter swaps in DNA to help explain how humans and chimp brains drifted apart in their evolution. But the new study highlights that creatures can rack up genome changes in other ways, says Giorgia Modenini, an evolutionary biologist at the University of Padua in Italy who was not involved with this research.
paras.zh: 研究人员此前曾研究过 DNA 中的单字母交换，以帮助解释人类和黑猩猩的大脑在进化过程中如何渐行渐远。但意大利帕多瓦大学的进化生物学家乔吉亚·莫德尼尼（Giorgia Modenini）表示，这项新研究强调生物可以通过其他方式积累基因组变化，他没有参与这项研究。

paras.en: The researchers do a convincing job of showing that these particular viral leftovers influence developmental differences between human and chimp neurons, says Ravinder Kanda, an evolutionary geneticist at Oxford Brookes University in Oxford, England. “They’ve proved that absolutely. How far that goes, I don’t think we can quite say yet.”
paras.zh: 英国牛津布鲁克斯大学的进化遗传学家 Ravinder Kanda 表示，研究人员做了令人信服的工作，证明这些特殊的病毒残留物会影响人类和黑猩猩神经元之间的发育差异。 “他们已经完全证明了这一点。我认为我们还不能说到底能走多远。”

paras.en: It could be that other controls on genes’ activity are also involved or that this particular ancient lever-puller may represent just a sliver of the viral holdovers that have shaped brain development, Kanda says. “I think there are many, many more retroviruses to be discovered, and at the moment we’ve only touched the tip of the iceberg.”
paras.zh: 坎达说，可能还涉及对基因活动的其他控制，或者这个特殊的古老拉杆器可能只是影响大脑发育的病毒残留物的一小部分。 “我认为还有很多很多的逆转录病毒有待发现，而目前我们只触及了冰山一角。”

articles.title: Your Brain May Be Switching Between Two Versions of Reality 15 Times a Second
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: How grounded do you feel in the present moment? It may be a little less than you think.
paras.zh: 你现在感觉有多踏实？它可能比你想象的要少一点。

paras.en: Even as you fix your gaze on the screen in front of you to read these words, your brain may be flickering between what you're consciously taking in and other visual information that never quite reaches your awareness.
paras.zh: 即使当您将目光固定在面前的屏幕上阅读这些文字时，您的大脑也可能会在您有意识地吸收的内容和其他从未完全达到您意识的视觉信息之间闪烁。

paras.en: A new preprint study involving both macaque monkeys and humans suggests that the brain may be switching back and forth between conscious and unconscious information around 15 times a second – raising the strange possibility that something other than visual availability is guiding your conscious experience of the world.
paras.zh: 一项涉及猕猴和人类的新预印本研究表明，大脑可能每秒在有意识和无意识信息之间来回切换大约 15 次，这提出了一种奇怪的可能性：除了视觉可用性之外，还有其他东西在指导你对世界的有意识体验。

paras.en: "At any moment, only some of the brain's activity reaches conscious awareness, while the rest is processed without ever being experienced," writes a team led by neuroscientists Janis Hesse and Doris Tsao of the University of California, Berkeley.
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校的神经科学家 Janis Hesse 和 Doris Tsao 领导的团队写道：“在任何时刻，只有部分大脑活动达到了有意识的意识，而其余的活动则在没有经历过的情况下进行了处理。”

paras.en: "How this division arises is among the most basic unsolved problems in neuroscience."
paras.zh: “这种分裂是如何产生的，是神经科学中最基本的未解决问题之一。”

paras.en: There are many things our bodies just do automatically, and sensing is one of them. We move through the world under a constant barrage of sensory information, and we cannot turn off our ability to take it in.
paras.zh: 我们的身体会自动做很多事情，感知就是其中之一。我们在不断涌现的感官信息的包围下穿梭于这个世界，我们无法关闭吸收这些信息的能力。

paras.en: What our brains can do is deprioritize some of that information. The famous example is your nose. It's always sitting bang in the middle of your field of view, but your brain mostly tunes it out. You know it's there; you don't need your eyes to keep confirming it.
paras.zh: 我们的大脑能做的就是降低某些信息的优先级。著名的例子就是你的鼻子。它总是出现在你的视野中央，但你的大脑基本上不会注意到它。你知道它就在那里；你不需要你的眼睛不断地确认它。

paras.en: This is obviously extremely useful. Without it, we'd be overwhelmed by the sheer volume of sensory input our brains receive.
paras.zh: 这显然是非常有用的。如果没有它，我们就会被大脑接收到的大量感官输入所淹没。

paras.en: But it also raises a huge question: How does the brain determine which information we consciously experience, and which information remains hidden from awareness?
paras.zh: 但这也提出了一个巨大的问题：大脑如何确定我们有意识地体验哪些信息，以及哪些信息仍然隐藏在意识之外？

paras.en: To seek answers, neuroscientists have spent decades studying which parts of the brain become active when stimuli are being consciously perceived. Over time, however, a problem emerged. The same parts of the brain can respond to unconscious stimuli, too.
paras.zh: 为了寻求答案，神经科学家花了几十年的时间研究当有意识地感知刺激时大脑的哪些部分会变得活跃。然而，随着时间的推移，问题出现了。大脑的相同部分也可以对无意识的刺激做出反应。

paras.en: Hesse and his colleagues asked a new question. What if those searches were focused on the wrong dimension?
paras.zh: 黑塞和他的同事提出了一个新问题。如果这些搜索集中在错误的维度怎么办？

paras.en: What if the answer lay not in space, but time?
paras.zh: 如果答案不在于空间，而在于时间呢？

paras.en: In other words, they thought the way brain activity changed over time might yield clues about how the brain handles conscious and unconscious visual information.
paras.zh: 换句话说，他们认为大脑活动随时间变化的方式可能会提供有关大脑如何处理有意识和无意识视觉信息的线索。

paras.en: Their research focused on macaques. Macaques wearing anaglyph glasses.
paras.zh: 他们的研究重点是猕猴。戴着浮雕眼镜的猕猴。

paras.en: You're probably familiar with the glasses that have one red lens and one cyan lens, used to trick your eyes into thinking you are seeing a 3D image.
paras.zh: 您可能熟悉这种眼镜，它有一个红色镜片和一个青色镜片，用于欺骗您的眼睛，让您认为正在看到 3D 图像。

paras.en: The same system can be exploited to show your eyes two different images. The eye looking through a cyan lens can see a red image but not a cyan one, and the eye looking through a red lens can see a cyan image but not a red one.
paras.zh: 可以利用同一个系统向您的眼睛显示两个不同的图像。通过青色镜片的眼睛可以看到红色图像，但看不到青色图像，而通过红色镜片的眼睛可以看到青色图像，但看不到红色图像。

paras.en: The researchers used this trick to show the macaques two different faces. First, they presented one face to one eye. Then, while that image remained in place, they suddenly introduced a second face to the other eye.
paras.zh: 研究人员利用这个技巧向猕猴展示了两张不同的面孔。首先，他们将一张脸呈现给一只眼睛。然后，当该图像保留在原处时，他们突然向另一只眼睛引入了第二张脸。

paras.en: Here's where things get weird. Rather than seeing both faces at once, the brain tends to prioritize the newly introduced face, suppressing the first from conscious awareness.
paras.zh: 这就是事情变得奇怪的地方。大脑不会同时看到两张脸，而是倾向于优先考虑新出现的脸，从而抑制第一张脸的意识。

paras.en: The first face hasn't gone anywhere. The eye is still receiving it. But the brain is no longer bringing it into conscious perception.
paras.zh: 第一张脸还没有消失。眼睛还在接收它。但大脑不再将其带入意识感知中。

paras.en: This phenomenon is called binocular flash suppression; it's a very useful tool that neuroscientists studying conscious and unconscious visual processing have been using for decades.
paras.zh: 这种现象称为双眼闪光抑制；这是研究有意识和无意识视觉处理的神经科学家几十年来一直使用的一个非常有用的工具。

paras.en: Now, the macaques couldn't tell the researchers which of the two images they were consciously perceiving, so humans were recruited to test the technique and confirm that it was the second image that dominated conscious perception.
paras.zh: 现在，猕猴无法告诉研究人员它们正在有意识地感知这两个图像中的哪一个，因此招募人类来测试该技术并确认这是第二个图像主导了有意识的感知。

paras.en: Once the researchers had confirmed that the technique worked as expected, they turned their attention to the macaques' brains.
paras.zh: 一旦研究人员确认该技术按预期发挥作用，他们就把注意力转向猕猴的大脑。

paras.en: Using tiny electrodes inserted into regions involved in visual processing, they recorded the electrical activity of hundreds of neurons simultaneously as the monkeys watched the competing images.
paras.zh: 他们利用插入视觉处理区域的微型电极，在猴子观看竞争图像时同时记录了数百个神经元的电活动。

paras.en: They were particularly interested in regions that specialize in recognizing faces. Here, they identified two distinct patterns of brain activity: one linked to the first face and the other to the second face.
paras.zh: 他们对专门识别面孔的区域特别感兴趣。在这里，他们发现了两种不同的大脑活动模式：一种与第一张脸相关，另一种与第二张脸相关。

paras.en: Interestingly, a pattern emerged in time, too.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，随着时间的推移，一种模式也出现了。

paras.en: Even though the second face was expected to remain dominant in conscious perception, the neurons didn't continuously represent that face. Instead, their activity rapidly alternated between the consciously perceived face and the one suppressed from awareness.
paras.zh: 尽管第二张脸预计将在意识感知中保持主导地位，但神经元并不能持续代表那张脸。相反，他们的活动在有意识地感知到的面孔和被意识抑制的面孔之间快速交替。

paras.en: This switching occurred around 15 times every second.
paras.zh: 这种切换每秒大约发生 15 次。

paras.en: So, even though the second face was expected to dominate the macaques' perception, the first face kept flickering through their brains.
paras.zh: 因此，尽管第二张脸预计将主导猕猴的感知，但第一张脸却不断在它们的大脑中闪烁。

paras.en: And the researchers found something else intriguing. During conscious moments, neurons responded more sharply to the features of the perceived face than to features of the suppressed face during the suppressed moments, suggesting that the brain may have a way of distinguishing between the two, even as it alternates between them.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现了一些其他有趣的事情。在有意识的时刻，神经元对感知到的面部特征的反应比在抑制时刻对被抑制的面部特征的反应更敏锐，这表明大脑可能有一种方法来区分两者，即使它在两者之间交替。

paras.en: The findings do not explain how the brain decides which information reaches consciousness, but the researchers speculate that the process allows the brain to sort through alternative visual information without altering current behavior. Such a process might allow us to continue navigating the world while our brains unobtrusively consider other interpretations of what we're seeing.
paras.zh: 研究结果并没有解释大脑如何决定哪些信息到达意识，但研究人员推测，这个过程允许大脑在不改变当前行为的情况下对替代视觉信息进行分类。这样的过程可能会让我们继续探索世界，同时我们的大脑不引人注意地考虑对我们所看到的事物的其他解释。

paras.en: There are also some important limitations. The study involved only two macaques, and they couldn't report what they were seeing, so their conscious perception had to be inferred from the human experiments. Additionally, the researchers only investigated specific regions involved in visual processing, not the entire brain.
paras.zh: 还有一些重要的限制。这项研究只涉及两只猕猴，它们无法报告自己所看到的内容，因此它们的意识感知必须从人体实验中推断出来。此外，研究人员只研究了涉及视觉处理的特定区域，而不是整个大脑。

paras.en: Nevertheless, the results raise a fascinating possibility – that our apparently seamless experience of the world is facilitated by furious, complex neural activity taking place behind the closed doors of our conscious experience.
paras.zh: 然而，结果提出了一种令人着迷的可能性——我们对世界的无缝体验是由我们意识体验的紧闭之门背后发生的激烈、复杂的神经活动促进的。

paras.en: "Identifying the mechanisms that orchestrate these transitions, and determining why only some temporal segments become available to awareness, will be essential for understanding how temporal population dynamics give rise to conscious perception," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“确定协调这些转变的机制，并确定为什么只有一些时间片段可以被意识所利用，对于理解时间群体动态如何产生意识感知至关重要。”

paras.en: The findings, yet to be peer-reviewed, are available on bioRxiv.
paras.zh: 该研究结果尚未经过同行评审，可在 bioRxiv 上获取。

articles.title: Physically Touching Your Dog Can Help Protect You From Upcoming Stress, Study Suggests
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: The amazing thing about our pets isn't just the wonderful relationships we get to have with them.
paras.zh: 我们的宠物令人惊奇的不仅仅是我们与它们之间的美好关系。

paras.en: These beautiful creatures are actually good for us too, with research showing that petting your dog or cat can lower stress levels, and it's even an effect we can see in the brain.
paras.zh: 这些美丽的生物实际上对我们也有好处，研究表明抚摸你的狗或猫可以降低压力水平，甚至我们可以在大脑中看到这种效果。

paras.en: But while the health perks of pet ownership are well known, there's still a lot we don't fully understand about how they emerge.
paras.zh: 尽管养宠物对健康的好处众所周知，但我们仍然不完全了解它们是如何产生的。

paras.en: In a new study in Biological Psychology, researchers from the University of Innsbruck in Austria looked into the phenomenon, and their findings suggest that physical touch could be key to the positive effects animals can provide.
paras.zh: 在《生物心理学》的一项新研究中，奥地利因斯布鲁克大学的研究人员对这一现象进行了研究，他们的发现表明，身体接触可能是动物产生积极影响的关键。

paras.en: "Pets enhance their owners' affect and well-being, providing tangible benefits that extend beyond their original utilitarian roles," explains a paper led by first author and psychology researcher Vanessa Kaufmann.
paras.zh: 第一作者、心理学研究员凡妮莎·考夫曼 (Vanessa Kaufmann) 领导的一篇论文解释道：“宠物可以增强主人的情感和幸福感，提供超越其最初功利角色的切实好处。”

paras.en: "Building on these insights, we sought to elucidate the psychobiological mechanisms through which such benefits arise."
paras.zh: “基于这些见解，我们试图阐明产生这些益处的心理生物学机制。”

paras.en: Human-to-human touch is known to reduce feelings of anxiety and stress, with research showing physical contact can lower heart rate and cortisol responses.
paras.zh: 众所周知，人与人之间的接触可以减少焦虑和压力的感觉，研究表明身体接触可以降低心率和皮质醇反应。

paras.en: A lot of studies have examined the well-being benefits of pet ownership, but physical touch has rarely been isolated as a standalone factor, meaning we don't have firm evidence for how it specifically might lower stress compared to other kinds of human-animal interactions.
paras.zh: 许多研究都检验了养宠物对健康的好处，但身体接触很少被孤立作为一个独立因素，这意味着我们没有确凿的证据证明与其他类型的人与动物互动相比，它如何具体降低压力。

paras.en: To explore further, Kaufmann and fellow researchers conducted an experiment with 64 adult dog owners (51 women, 13 men, average age 34.1) and their dogs, who were all healthy and at least two years old.
paras.zh: 为了进一步探索，考夫曼和其他研究人员对 64 名成年狗主人（51 名女性，13 名男性，平均年龄 34.1 岁）及其狗进行了一项实验，这些狗都健康且至少两岁。

paras.en: In the experiment, dog owners were subjected to tests designed to raise their stress levels, while their stress responses were monitored by electrocardiography (ECG) and electroencephalography (EEG).
paras.zh: 在实验中，狗主人接受了旨在提高其压力水平的测试，同时通过心电图（ECG）和脑电图（EEG）监测他们的压力反应。

paras.en: The stress tests involved answering general knowledge questions within strict time limits, or performing an arithmetic exercise where they had to count down from a given number in fixed numerical steps.
paras.zh: 压力测试包括在严格的时间限制内回答常识问题，或者进行算术练习，他们必须以固定的数字步长从给定的数字开始倒数。

paras.en: While performing the tasks, they were remotely monitored by an evaluator, who gave them negative feedback on how they were doing.
paras.zh: 在执行任务时，评估员对他们进行远程监控，评估员对他们的表现给出负面反馈。

paras.en: After a round of this, the participants took a 5-minute recovery period in which they could freely touch and physically interact with their dog if they wanted to, or were prevented from doing so, due to the dog being leashed and out of reach.
paras.zh: 一轮结束后，参与者需要 5 分钟的恢复时间，在此期间，如果他们愿意，他们可以自由地触摸他们的狗并与他们进行身体互动，但由于狗被拴着并且无法触及，他们无法这样做。

paras.en: Once the recovery period ended, participants had to undergo a second round of the stress test.
paras.zh: 恢复期结束后，参与者必须接受第二轮压力测试。

paras.en: The experiment produced some interesting results.
paras.zh: 该实验产生了一些有趣的结果。

paras.en: As was expected, the general knowledge and arithmetic tests triggered signs of biological stress in the participants, with the ECG measurements showing increased heart rates and reduced heart rate variability.
paras.zh: 正如预期的那样，常识和算术测试引发了参与者的生物压力迹象，心电图测量显示心率增加和心率变异性降低。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the EEG indicated alpha brain waves (associated with relaxation) were suppressed by the stress test, while beta brain wave activity was increased, indicating greater cognitive arousal.
paras.zh: 与此同时，脑电图显示，压力测试抑制了α脑电波（与放松相关），而β脑电波活动增加，表明认知唤醒程度更高。

paras.en: Contrary to the researchers' expectations, though, the dog owners who were able to physically interact with their pets didn't appear to recover more quickly from the stress during the recovery period.
paras.zh: 然而，与研究人员的预期相反，能够与宠物进行身体互动的狗主人在恢复期间似乎并没有从压力中恢复得更快。

paras.en: But their ability to touch and pet their dog during that 5-minute window did produce one significant benefit.
paras.zh: 但他们在这 5 分钟的时间里触摸和抚摸狗的能力确实产生了一个显着的好处。

paras.en: The participants who had physically interacted with their dog during the break showed lower signs of stress during the second round of the stress test, suggesting that touching their pet buffered them from future stress they were about to experience.
paras.zh: 在休息期间与狗进行身体互动的参与者在第二轮压力测试中表现出较低的压力迹象，这表明触摸他们的宠物可以缓冲他们未来即将经历的压力。

paras.en: "These results indicate that touching one's dog dampens the bodily impact of an upcoming stressor and that pet owners may naturally seek such touch when interacting with their pet," the researchers explain.
paras.zh: 研究人员解释说：“这些结果表明，触摸狗可以减轻即将到来的压力源对身体的影响，宠物主人在与宠物互动时可能会自然地寻求这种触摸。”

paras.en: "Thus, touch may represent an important mechanistic pathway through which upcoming threats are experienced as less threatening, potentially contributing to broader benefits for pet-owner well-being."
paras.zh: “因此，触摸可能代表了一种重要的机制途径，通过这种途径，即将到来的威胁会被认为威胁较小，从而可能为宠物主人的福祉带来更广泛的好处。”

paras.en: Interestingly, the participants' own ratings of how much stress they felt during the experiment didn't reflect the physiological changes measured by the researchers, suggesting that some of the effects of interacting with pets might occur without us consciously noticing them.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，参与者自己在实验过程中感受到的压力程度并没有反映研究人员测量的生理变化，这表明与宠物互动的一些影响可能会在我们没有意识到的情况下发生。

paras.en: But don't let that stop you from patting your nearest and dearest if they're close at hand.
paras.zh: 但不要因此而阻止你拍拍你最亲近的人（如果他们就在你身边）。

paras.en: In its own invisible way, that gesture of affection might help protect you from whatever stress is coming your way next.
paras.zh: 以一种无形的方式，这种关爱的姿态可能会帮助你免受接下来即将到来的任何压力。

paras.en: And even if it doesn't, they'll love you for it.
paras.zh: 即使没有，他们也会因此而爱你。

paras.en: The findings are reported in Biological Psychology.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《生物心理学》上。

articles.title: NASA's Perseverance Just Broke The Off-World Driving Record, While Mostly Steering Itself
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: When we look up at Mars, many millions of miles away, it's inspiring to think that someone may be looking back at us – not any heat-ray-equipped aliens, thankfully, but one of humanity's greatest accomplishments: NASA's Perseverance rover.
paras.zh: 当我们仰望数百万英里之外的火星时，令人振奋的是，有人可能正在回头看我们——谢天谢地，不是任何配备热射线的外星人，而是人类最伟大的成就之一：美国宇航局的毅力号火星车。

paras.en: In July of 2020, the affectionately nicknamed Percy left Earth forever in a bright flash of hope during some of modern history's darkest days.
paras.zh: 2020 年 7 月，在现代历史上最黑暗的日子里，被亲切地昵称为“珀西”的他带着一丝希望永远离开了地球。

paras.en: It, and we, have come a long way since then.
paras.zh: 从那时起，它和我们已经取得了长足的进步。

paras.en: In fact, Perseverance has recently achieved something completely unique: it has traveled farther across the surface of another world than any previous entity.
paras.zh: 事实上，毅力号最近取得了一些完全独特的成果：它在另一个世界的表面上行驶得比以前的任何实体都更远。

paras.en: As its interplanetary odometer ticked off 45.22 kilometers (28.10 miles) on October 11, it graciously surpassed the record set by its older sibling Opportunity, which traversed 45.16 kilometers of dusty, red, rocky Martian expanse from 2004 to 2018.
paras.zh: 10 月 11 日，当它的行星际里程计达到 45.22 公里（28.10 英里）时，它轻松地超越了它的老兄弟机遇号创下的纪录，后者在 2004 年至 2018 年期间穿越了 45.16 公里的尘土飞扬、红色、岩石遍布的火星。

paras.en: Perseverance is a product of its predecessors. It has covered more than 90 percent of its record-breaking distance through its own wits, using its AutoNav system to scan and safely scale the wild terrain between waypoints set by scientists on Earth.
paras.zh: 毅力是前人的产物。它通过自己的智慧完成了超过 90% 的破纪录距离，利用其 AutoNav 系统扫描并安全地缩放地球上科学家设定的航路点之间的野生地形。

paras.en: This feat was made possible by the twin rovers Opportunity and Spirit, which completed around 5 percent of their distance using the earliest AutoNav system.
paras.zh: 这一壮举是由机遇号和勇气号双火星车实现的，它们使用最早的 AutoNav 系统完成了大约 5% 的距离。

paras.en: Perseverance's most prototypical predecessor, and the first rover on Mars, was a dog-sized explorer named Sojourner, which landed in 1997 and covered around 100 meters.
paras.zh: 毅力号最典型的前身，也是火星上的第一辆漫游车，是一个名为 Sojourner 的狗大小的探测器，它于 1997 年登陆，覆盖了约 100 米。

paras.en: And while Sojourner took 20 measurement points of the path ahead of it, Perseverance processes 200,000 with each glance, JPL scientists point out.
paras.zh: 喷气推进实验室的科学家指出，“旅居者号”对前方路径进行了 20 个测量点，而“毅力号”则每次扫视都会处理 200,000 个测量点。

paras.en: It can do this at or near its top speed, "thinking while driving" to cover as much as a blistering 412 meters (1,351 feet) in a single sol, or Martian day, which is about 40 minutes longer than an Earth day.
paras.zh: 它可以以或接近最高速度做到这一点，“边开车边思考”，在一个太阳日或火星日（即比地球日长约 40 分钟）内行驶 412 米（1,351 英尺）的距离。

paras.en: Perseverance has also provided a real 'Wright Brothers moment' with its Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, the first controlled aircraft flown on another planet.
paras.zh: 毅力号还凭借其独创性火星直升机提供了真正的“莱特兄弟时刻”，这是第一架在另一个星球上飞行的受控飞机。

paras.en: Instead of performing five test flights in 30 days, it shattered everyone's hopes. In a good way, because it made 72 flights across three years, covering 17 kilometers and lifting itself nearly 24 meters in Mars' whisper-thin atmosphere.
paras.zh: 30天内没有进行5次试飞，反而让大家的希望破灭了。这是一件好事，因为它在三年内进行了 72 次飞行，飞行里程达 17 公里，在火星稀薄的大气层中上升了近 24 米。

paras.en: Perseverance's current objective is skirting Jezero Crater, so it's in the Lac de Charmes region, which may one day be the wine-growing part of Mars.
paras.zh: 毅力号当前的目标是绕过杰泽罗陨石坑，因此它位于查尔姆湖地区，该地区有一天可能会成为火星上的葡萄酒产区。

paras.en: It's exploring some of the oldest rocks we've ever laid eyes, lasers, or robotic arms upon – "probably older than 4 billion years," says Ken Farley, professor of geochemistry at Caltech and former Perseverance project scientist.
paras.zh: 它正在探索一些我们用眼睛、激光或机械臂见过的最古老的岩石——“可能有超过 40 亿年的历史”，加州理工学院地球化学教授、前毅力项目科学家肯·法利 (Ken Farley) 说。

paras.en: "There are few rocks on Earth older than 4 billion years. So we are in an area that is very deep in the history of the solar system."
paras.zh: “地球上很少有岩石的年龄超过 40 亿年。因此，我们所处的区域在太阳系的历史中非常深厚。”

paras.en: On Earth, most rocks of such an ancient age have been disintegrated by erosion or recycled by plate tectonics. Yet some remain, and may hold traces of early life.
paras.zh: 在地球上，大多数如此古老的岩石已经因侵蚀而分解或被板块构造回收。然而有些仍然存在，并且可能保留着早期生命的痕迹。

paras.en: Of course, this may be the ultimate goal for Perseverance. And it has found what may be the best evidence for extraterrestrial biology yet, trapped within the leopard-spot speckled rock called Cheyava Falls, in an ancient asteroid-gouged basin that held water several billion years ago.
paras.zh: 当然，这或许就是毅力的最终目标。它发现了可能是迄今为止外星生物的最佳证据，这些证据被困在被称为切亚瓦瀑布的豹斑斑点岩石中，该岩石位于一个古老的小行星凿凿盆地中，数十亿年前就有水。

paras.en: Perseverance is now on the western rim of Jezero Crater in Lac de Charmes, on its way to check out Idubi, which may have been a hydrothermal system, possibly similar to those thought to have helped life arise on Earth.
paras.zh: 毅力号现在位于查姆湖的杰泽罗陨石坑西缘，正在前往检查伊杜比的途中，伊杜比可能是一个热液系统，可能类似于那些被认为帮助地球上生命诞生的系统。

paras.en: Rainbow Falls is another revealing target: a chunk of Mars ripped out of the ground by the impact that created Jezero Crater.
paras.zh: 彩虹瀑布是另一个具有启发性的目标：在形成杰泽罗陨石坑的撞击中，火星的一大块从地面上被撕裂出来。

paras.en: Perseverance therefore presents a contrast. Searching for life signs from faraway exoplanets is essential, but rife with challenges, as shown by the highly disputed 'biosignature' from K2-18b, or the more locally famous but equally fickle phosphine from Venus.
paras.zh: 因此，毅力呈现出对比。从遥远的系外行星中寻找生命迹象是必要的，但也充满了挑战，正如来自 K2-18b 的备受争议的“生物特征”，或者来自金星的当地更著名但同样变化无常的磷化氢所表明的那样。

paras.en: As Farley suggests, "the place that will give the richest information is the one you can bring samples from."
paras.zh: 正如法利所说，“提供最丰富信息的地方就是你可以带样品的地方。”

paras.en: A return mission is the obvious next step, though NASA's Mars Sample Return program lost its funding earlier this year, leaving the timing of any retrieval uncertain.
paras.zh: 尽管美国宇航局的火星样本返回计划在今年早些时候失去了资金，导致任何回收的时间都不确定，但返回任务显然是下一步。

paras.en: Since Mars was a wet planet when life evolved on Earth, collected samples can help answer the most profound existential question – the evidence is 'bagged' and waiting just down our cosmic street.
paras.zh: 由于当生命在地球上进化时，火星是一个潮湿的星球，收集的样本可以帮助回答最深刻的存在问题——证据已经“装袋”，就在我们的宇宙街上等待着。

paras.en: Such a mission would also inform future efforts to convey humans to the red planet and back, safe and sound, sacrificing only their squat and bench press numbers.
paras.zh: 这样的任务还将为未来将人类安全无恙地运送到红色星球并返回的努力提供信息，而仅牺牲他们的深蹲和卧推次数。

paras.en: Finally, if anyone feels wistful for Percy spending cold nights alone on a faraway world, consider that our emissary has seen stunning sunsets, glimpsed green-glowing auroras, and, perhaps, been the first to see signs of another lineage of life in the Solar System.
paras.zh: 最后，如果有人渴望珀西独自在遥远的世界度过寒冷的夜晚，请考虑一下我们的使者已经看到了令人惊叹的日落，瞥见了绿色发光的极光，并且也许是第一个看到太阳系中另一种生命谱系迹象的人。

paras.en: Not a bad haul, and a privilege passed to us.
paras.zh: 收获不错，我们也获得了这样的特权。

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising double benefit of exercise for Parkinson’s

paras.en: Scientists discover a surprising double benefit of exercise for Parkinsonâs
paras.zh: 科学家发现运动对帕金森病有惊人的双重好处

paras.en: - A seven-year study found that people with Parkinsonâs disease who were more physically active experienced slower declines in memory, thinking, and movement abilities. Those exercising more than eight hours per week showed almost no average cognitive decline, suggesting that staying active may offer important benefits as the disease progresses.
paras.zh: - 一项为期七年的研究发现，患有帕金森病的人如果身体活动较多，记忆力、思维和运动能力的下降速度会较慢。那些每周锻炼超过八小时的人几乎没有表现出平均认知能力下降，这表明随着疾病的进展，保持活跃可能会带来重要的好处。

paras.en: People with Parkinson's disease who are more physically active may experience slower declines in memory, thinking, and movement, according to a new study published October 7, 2026, in Neurology, the official medical journal of the American Academy of Neurology.
paras.zh: 根据 2026 年 10 月 7 日发表在美国神经病学学会官方医学杂志《神经病学》上的一项新研究，如果帕金森病患者体力活动较多，记忆力、思维和运动能力的下降可能会较慢。

paras.en: The findings suggest that staying active could offer two important advantages for people living with Parkinson's. However, researchers emphasize that the study identified a connection between physical activity and slower symptom progression. It does not establish that exercise directly causes the disease to progress more slowly.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，保持活跃可以为帕金森病患者带来两个重要的优势。然而，研究人员强调，该研究发现体力活动与症状进展缓慢之间存在联系。它并不能确定运动直接导致疾病进展得更慢。

paras.en: "Parkinson's disease is a brain disorder that causes movement and cognitive problems that gradually worsen leading to disability and a loss of independence," said study author Dong-Woo Ryu, MD, PhD, of the University of Cincinnati in Ohio. "Previous research has shown associations between physical activity and movement symptoms. Our study found physical activity may have dual benefits, with associations with slower declines in movement and cognition."
paras.zh: 研究作者、俄亥俄州辛辛那提大学的 Dong-Woo Ryu 博士说：“帕金森病是一种脑部疾病，会导致运动和认知问题，并逐渐恶化，导致残疾和丧失独立性。” “之前的研究已经表明体力活动和运动症状之间存在关联。我们的研究发现体力活动可能具有双重好处，与运动和认知能力下降的速度减缓有关。”

paras.en: Tracking Exercise and Parkinson's Symptoms Over Seven Years
paras.zh: 七年来追踪运动和帕金森症状

paras.en: The research involved 294 adults with mild to moderate Parkinson's disease. Participants were 66 years old on average, and researchers monitored their health for up to seven years.
paras.zh: 该研究涉及 294 名患有轻度至中度帕金森病的成年人。参与者平均年龄 66 岁，研究人员对他们的健康状况进行了长达七年的监测。

paras.en: To understand their activity habits, participants completed questionnaires estimating how many hours each week they spent being physically active. The questions covered activities performed at work, around the home, and during hobbies or recreation.
paras.zh: 为了了解他们的活动习惯，参与者完成了问卷调查，估算他们每周花多少时间进行身体活动。这些问题涵盖了工作中、家庭周围以及爱好或娱乐期间进行的活动。

paras.en: Researchers classified activities by their intensity. Moderate activities included brisk walking, doubles tennis, leisurely swimming, and household tasks such as cleaning windows, vacuuming, or mowing the lawn. More demanding activities included running, cycling at higher speeds, participating in team sports, playing singles tennis, shoveling, and carrying heavy objects.
paras.zh: 研究人员根据活动的强度对活动进行分类。适度的活动包括快走、网球双打、悠闲游泳以及清洁窗户、吸尘或修剪草坪等家务劳动。要求更高的活动包括跑步、高速骑自行车、参加团队运动、打单打网球、铲土和搬运重物。

paras.en: The team examined physical activity in three ways. First, they calculated the total time participants spent doing moderate or vigorous activities. Second, they estimated overall activity volume by combining duration with intensity, giving greater weight to strenuous exercise. Third, they separately measured the amount of time spent doing vigorous activities.
paras.zh: 研究小组通过三种方式检查身体活动。首先，他们计算了参与者进行中等或剧烈活动所花费的总时间。其次，他们通过结合持续时间和强度来估计总体活动量，并给予剧烈运动更大的权重。第三，他们分别测量了进行剧烈活动所花费的时间。

paras.en: Based on total weekly activity time, participants were placed into three categories. Those in the least active group reported up to four hours per week, the moderately active group reported four to eight hours, and the most active group reported more than eight hours.
paras.zh: 根据每周总活动时间，参与者被分为三类。活动最少的组报告每周最多四小时，中等活动的组报告每周四到八小时，最活跃的组报告每周超过八小时。

paras.en: Each year, participants also completed assessments designed to track changes in thinking and memory, along with tests evaluating the severity of their Parkinson's symptoms.
paras.zh: 每年，参与者还完成旨在跟踪思维和记忆变化的评估，以及评估帕金森症状严重程度的测试。

paras.en: More Activity Linked to Slower Memory Decline
paras.zh: 活动越多，记忆力衰退速度越慢

paras.en: One of the most striking differences emerged in cognitive performance. Researchers used a 30-point test of thinking and memory, with lower scores reflecting poorer cognitive function.
paras.zh: 最显着的差异之一出现在认知表现上。研究人员对思维和记忆进行了 30 分的测试，分数较低反映出认知功能较差。

paras.en: Among participants in the least active group, scores fell by an estimated average of 0.478 points each year. The moderately active group experienced a much smaller annual decline of 0.090 points.
paras.zh: 在最不活跃组的参与者中，估计分数每年平均下降 0.478 分。中等活跃组的年度跌幅要小得多，为 0.090 点。

paras.en: For the most active participants, the estimated average yearly decrease was only 0.007 points, indicating that their cognitive scores remained nearly unchanged over time.
paras.zh: 对于最活跃的参与者来说，估计平均每年下降仅 0.007 分，这表明他们的认知得分随着时间的推移几乎保持不变。

paras.en: The researchers also examined changes in Parkinson's movement symptoms using an assessment scored from zero to 132. Higher numbers represented more severe symptoms, and participants began the study with an average score of 23.
paras.zh: 研究人员还使用从 0 到 132 的评估分数来检查帕金森氏症运动症状的变化。数字越高代表症状越严重，参与者开始研究时的平均分数为 23。

paras.en: In the least active group, symptom scores increased by an estimated 0.143 points annually, indicating a slight worsening. By contrast, scores decreased by 0.225 points per year in the moderately active group and by 0.783 points in the most active group.
paras.zh: 在最不活跃的组中，症状评分每年增加约 0.143 分，表明症状略有恶化。相比之下，中等活动组的分数每年下降 0.225 分，最活跃组的分数每年下降 0.783 分。

paras.en: Even after accounting for participants' age, sex, and how long they had been living with Parkinson's, the researchers found that the most active group experienced slower cognitive decline and less worsening of movement symptoms than the least active group.
paras.zh: 即使考虑了参与者的年龄、性别以及他们患有帕金森病的时间，研究人员发现，与最不活跃的群体相比，最活跃的群体认知能力下降较慢，运动症状恶化的程度也较轻。

paras.en: The connection was not limited to one measure of exercise. Higher total activity time, greater overall activity volume, and more time spent exercising vigorously were each associated with slower deterioration in both thinking abilities and movement symptoms.
paras.zh: 这种联系并不局限于一种锻炼措施。总活动时间越长、总活动量越大、剧烈运动时间越长，都与思维能力和运动症状恶化速度减慢相关。

paras.en: Why Consistent Physical Activity May Matter
paras.zh: 为什么持续的身体活动可能很重要

paras.en: The results suggest that remaining physically active over time could be especially important for people with Parkinson's disease. Researchers noted that even relatively small differences in the rate of decline might become more significant when they accumulate over several years.
paras.zh: 结果表明，随着时间的推移保持身体活动对于帕金森病患者尤其重要。研究人员指出，即使下降速度的差异相对较小，经过几年的积累，也可能变得更加显着。

paras.en: "The possible benefits of physical activity for people with Parkinson's disease may depend on how long they stay active and whether they continue exercising over time," said Ryu. "While our study found small differences between activity levels, these differences may become more meaningful over time. Since participants generally had good thinking and memory skills at the start of the study, our results should be interpreted with caution and further studies are needed."
paras.zh: Ryu 说：“体育活动对帕金森病患者可能带来的好处可能取决于他们保持活跃的时间以及他们是否继续锻炼。” “虽然我们的研究发现活动水平之间存在微小差异，但随着时间的推移，这些差异可能会变得更加有意义。由于参与者在研究开始时通常具有良好的思维和记忆能力，因此我们的结果应谨慎解释，并且需要进一步研究。”

paras.en: The researchers also identified an important limitation. Physical activity levels were based on participants' own reports rather than direct measurements, meaning some estimates may have been inaccurate.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现了一个重要的限制。身体活动水平是基于参与者自己的报告而不是直接测量，这意味着一些估计可能不准确。

paras.en: Although the findings strengthen the evidence connecting physical activity with better long-term outcomes in Parkinson's disease, additional research will be needed to determine whether exercise itself can slow the progression of symptoms.
paras.zh: 尽管这些发现强化了体力活动与帕金森病更好的长期结果联系起来的证据，但还需要进行更多的研究来确定运动本身是否可以减缓症状的进展。

paras.en: Funding for the study came from a grant provided by the Gardner Family Foundation and the Precision Medicine in Neurodegenerative Diseases Fund.
paras.zh: 该研究的资金来自加德纳家族基金会和神经退行性疾病精准医学基金提供的资助。

articles.title: A tiny defect in a crystal reveals a big quantum surprise

paras.en: A tiny defect in a crystal reveals a big quantum surprise
paras.zh: 晶体中的微小缺陷揭示了巨大的量子惊喜

paras.en: Scientists uncover a hidden energy-loss mechanism in silicon carbide that could unlock advances in quantum computing, sensing, and renewable energy technologies.
paras.zh: 科学家们发现了碳化硅中隐藏的能量损失机制，可以释放量子计算、传感和可再生能源技术的进步。

paras.en: - Researchers have solved a long-standing challenge in understanding how tiny defects in materials like diamond and silicon carbide behave when exposed to light. Their new computational method revealed a surprisingly important energy-loss mechanism in silicon carbide that scientists had previously underestimated. The finding helps explain a mystery that has puzzled researchers for years and could improve the design of quantum computers and sensors.
paras.zh: - Researchers have solved a long-standing challenge in understanding how tiny defects in materials like diamond and silicon carbide behave when exposed to light.他们的新计算方法揭示了碳化硅中一个令人惊讶的重要能量损失机制，而科学家之前却低估了这一机制。这一发现有助于解释多年来困扰研究人员的一个谜团，并可以改进量子计算机和传感器的设计。

paras.en: When light strikes a tiny imperfection inside a material such as diamond or silicon carbide, it can transfer energy to electrons and push them into an excited state. These imperfections, known as spin defects, could become valuable building blocks for future quantum technologies, including quantum sensors. Because they can function as stable qubits whose states can be read, scientists are eager to understand exactly how they behave. However, predicting how their energy changes over time has remained a major challenge.
paras.zh: 当光照射到金刚石或碳化硅等材料内部的微小缺陷时，它可以将能量传递给电子并将其推入激发态。这些缺陷被称为自旋缺陷，可能成为未来量子技术（包括量子传感器）的宝贵组成部分。因为它们可以充当稳定的量子位，其状态可以被读取，所以科学家们渴望确切地了解它们的行为方式。然而，预测它们的能量如何随时间变化仍然是一个重大挑战。

paras.en: Researchers at the University of Chicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering (UChicago PME) have now developed a computational method that provides a more complete picture of what happens when these defects interact with light. Their approach can simulate the entire optical cycle, including a particularly difficult process known as internal conversion.
paras.zh: 芝加哥大学普利兹克分子工程学院 (UChicago PME) 的研究人员现已开发出一种计算方法，可以更全面地了解这些缺陷与光相互作用时会发生什么。他们的方法可以模拟整个光学循环，包括称为内部转换的特别困难的过程。

paras.en: The findings, published in Physical Review Letters, could help scientists design better materials for quantum technologies. The method may also prove useful for studying materials involved in renewable energy conversion and storage.
paras.zh: 该研究结果发表在《物理评论快报》上，可以帮助科学家为量子技术设计更好的材料。该方法还可能有助于研究涉及可再生能源转换和存储的材料。

paras.en: "This internal conversion process is not only relevant to spin defects -- it's also related to processes of interest to energy technologies," said Giulia Galli, the Liew Family Professor of Electronic Structure and Simulations in UChicago PME and the Department of Chemistry and the senior author of the study. "That's one of the reasons this work is so exciting."
paras.zh: “这种内部转换过程不仅与自旋缺陷有关，还与能源技术感兴趣的过程有关，”芝加哥大学 PME 和化学系电子结构与模拟刘氏家族教授、该研究的资深作者 Giulia Galli 说。 “这就是这项工作如此令人兴奋的原因之一。”

paras.en: When a laser excites a spin defect, the defect can return to its original, lower-energy state through several different processes. It might release a photon of light, transition between states with different spins, or transfer its energy into vibrations of the surrounding atoms.
paras.zh: 当激光激发自旋缺陷时，该缺陷可以通过几个不同的过程返回到其原始的较低能量状态。它可能会释放光子，在不同自旋的状态之间跃迁，或者将其能量转移到周围原子的振动中。

paras.en: That final pathway, called internal conversion, has been especially difficult for scientists to model accurately. Although the fundamental equations of quantum mechanics can describe the other two processes, calculating how energy is lost through atomic vibrations presents substantial computational obstacles.
paras.zh: That final pathway, called internal conversion, has been especially difficult for scientists to model accurately.尽管量子力学的基本方程可以描述其他两个过程，但计算原子振动如何损失能量存在很大的计算障碍。

paras.en: "Although the equations are known, it's hard to describe the process accurately because of computational difficulties," said Stefano Villani, a UChicago PME postdoctoral researcher and the study's first author. "You need to account for complex interactions between the electrons and surrounding atoms, and that's challenging in realistic solids represented by models with hundreds or thousands of atoms"
paras.zh: “虽然方程是已知的，但由于计算困难，很难准确地描述这个过程，”芝加哥大学 PME 博士后研究员、该研究的第一作者 Stefano Villani 说。 “你需要考虑电子与周围原子之间复杂的相互作用，这在由数百或数千个原子模型代表的现实固体中具有挑战性”

paras.en: To overcome this problem, Galli, Villani, and Yu Jin combined several computational techniques that their research group had developed over many years. Jin, a former graduate student in Galli's group, is now a postdoctoral scholar at the Flatiron Institute in New York.
paras.zh: 为了克服这个问题，Galli、Villani 和 Yu Jin 结合了他们的研究小组多年来开发的几种计算技术。金曾是加利课题组的研究生，现在是纽约熨斗研究所的博士后学者。

paras.en: The researchers used mathematical descriptions known as many-body wavefunctions to represent the excited states of spin defects. Through exact mathematical derivations, they determined how strongly each excited state interacts with the movements of nearby atoms.
paras.zh: 研究人员使用称为多体波函数的数学描述来表示自旋缺陷的激发态。通过精确的数学推导，他们确定了每个激发态与附近原子运动相互作用的强度。

paras.en: This allowed them to calculate how individual electronic states connect with all the possible vibrational configurations of hundreds of surrounding atoms, rather than having to analyze those configurations individually.
paras.zh: 这使他们能够计算单个电子态如何与数百个周围原子的所有可能的振动配置相连接，而不必单独分析这些配置。

paras.en: "In the past, a clear mathematical derivation and efficient algorithms were not available," explained Yu Jin. "The new derivation came together after years of work on the optical cycle of spin defects."
paras.zh: “过去没有清晰的数学推导和高效的算法。”于进解释道。 “经过多年对自旋缺陷光学循环的研究，得出了新的推导结果。”

paras.en: The researchers incorporated their new framework into WEST, an open-source simulation program optimized for graphics processing units (GPUs). Galli's group has spent the past decade developing WEST through the Midwest Integrated Center for Computational Materials (MICCoM), which has received funding from the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Basic Energy Sciences since 2015.
paras.zh: 研究人员将他们的新框架纳入 WEST，这是一个针对图形处理单元 (GPU) 优化的开源模拟程序。 Galli 的团队在过去十年中通过中西部计算材料综合中心 (MICCoM) 开发 WEST，该中心自 2015 年以来一直获得美国能源部基础能源科学办公室的资助。

paras.en: A Surprising Discovery Inside Silicon Carbide
paras.zh: 碳化硅内部的惊人发现

paras.en: To test their approach, the researchers first examined a nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond, a type of crystal defect widely studied for quantum applications.
paras.zh: 为了测试他们的方法，研究人员首先检查了金刚石中的氮空位中心，这是一种为量子应用而广泛研究的晶体缺陷。

paras.en: Their calculations closely matched recent spectroscopy measurements. For triplet states, internal conversion contributed relatively little to energy loss. In singlet states, however, it was the primary mechanism responsible for releasing energy. Both findings agreed with what scientists had previously expected.
paras.zh: 他们的计算结果与最近的光谱测量结果非常吻合。对于三重态，内转换对能量损失的贡献相对较小。然而，在单线态下，它是释放能量的主要机制。这两项发现均符合科学家此前的预期。

paras.en: The results changed when the team investigated a divacancy defect in silicon carbide.
paras.zh: 当团队研究碳化硅中的双空位缺陷时，结果发生了变化。

paras.en: Their calculations revealed that internal conversion has a much greater influence on the lifetime of the defect's excited triplet state than earlier models had accounted for. This previously underestimated contribution helped explain a long-standing disagreement between theoretical predictions and experimental observations.
paras.zh: 他们的计算表明，内部转换对缺陷激发三重态寿命的影响比早期模型所解释的要大得多。这一先前被低估的贡献有助于解释理论预测和实验观察之间长期存在的分歧。

paras.en: "We were expecting to see an effect, but of a smaller magnitude," Galli said. "What we found is that this internal conversion process turns out to be more important than we thought."
paras.zh: “我们本来希望看到效果，但幅度较小，”加利说。“我们发现，这个内部转换过程比我们想象的更重要。”

paras.en: Understanding this unexpected energy-loss pathway could help scientists more accurately predict the behavior of silicon carbide defects and improve their potential use as qubits in future quantum devices.
paras.zh: 了解这种意想不到的能量损失途径可以帮助科学家更准确地预测碳化硅缺陷的行为，并提高它们在未来量子设备中作为量子位的潜在用途。

paras.en: A New Tool for Quantum Computing and Energy Research
paras.zh: 量子计算和能源研究的新工具

paras.en: With the framework now available through WEST, researchers at other institutions can begin applying it to their own studies. However, Galli noted that the simulations still demand considerable computing power.
paras.zh: 借助 WEST 现在提供的框架，其他机构的研究人员可以开始将其应用到自己的研究中。然而，加利指出，模拟仍然需要相当大的计算能力。

paras.en: The team is exploring ways to reduce those requirements, including the use of artificial intelligence.
paras.zh: 该团队正在探索减少这些要求的方法，包括使用人工智能。

paras.en: "We are working on ways to integrate machine learning into excited states calculations to further improve the efficiency of our method," Villani said.
paras.zh: “我们正在研究将机器学习集成到激发态计算中的方法，以进一步提高我们方法的效率，”维拉尼说。

paras.en: Meanwhile, the scientists are expanding their approach to investigate spin defects in silicon, as well as materials used in energy technologies where internal conversion influences how energy is transferred or lost.
paras.zh: 与此同时，科学家们正在扩展他们的方法来研究硅中的自旋缺陷，以及能源技术中使用的材料，其中内部转换会影响能量的转移或损失。

paras.en: By addressing one of the most difficult parts of modeling how spin defects respond to light, the researchers have made it possible to predict their behavior more completely and accurately.
paras.zh: 通过解决自旋缺陷如何响应光的建模中最困难的部分之一，研究人员可以更完整、更准确地预测它们的行为。

paras.en: "We provided the missing piece of the puzzle needed to completely describe the optical cycle of spin defects," Galli said. "Our work can now be used to make more accurate predictions about many materials of interest for quantum technologies," added Yu Jin.
paras.zh: 加利说：“我们提供了完整描述自旋缺陷光学循环所需的拼图中缺失的一块。” “我们的工作现在可以用来对量子技术感兴趣的许多材料做出更准确的预测，”于金补充道。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Chicago. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由芝加哥大学提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

articles.title: MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells

paras.en: MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院的科学家建造了一个利用活体肌肉细胞游泳的微型机器人

paras.en: - MIT engineers have built a paper-thin swimming robot powered by living muscle cells that respond to flashes of light, allowing it to swim and steer through water. The breakthrough could pave the way for tiny, self-healing biological robots capable of exploring fragile environments that ordinary machines cannot safely navigate.
paras.zh: - 麻省理工学院的工程师们建造了一种薄如纸的游泳机器人，由活体肌肉细胞提供动力，对闪光做出反应，使其能够在水中游泳和驾驶。这一突破可能为微型、自我修复的生物机器人铺平道路，这些机器人能够探索普通机器无法安全穿越的脆弱环境。

paras.en: A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water. MIT researchers have demonstrated that a single, carefully engineered layer of living muscle cells can generate enough force to propel a tiny robot forward.
paras.zh: 游泳机器人不一定需要笨重的电机或强大的机械部件来在水中移动。麻省理工学院的研究人员证明，精心设计的一层活体肌肉细胞可以产生足够的力量来推动微型机器人前进。

paras.en: The engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a new study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. The gel forms two fins, each coated with a layer of muscle cells far thinner than a human hair. These cells have been genetically modified to contract when exposed to light.
paras.zh: 工程师们开发了一种极其纤薄的游泳机器人，它利用活体肌肉组织来移动其鳍。在《先进功能材料》上发表的一项新研究中描述了该装置具有柔性凝胶框架，其长度和宽度大致相当于口香糖棒。凝胶形成两个鳍，每个鳍上都涂有一层比人类头发丝薄得多的肌肉细胞。这些细胞经过基因改造，在光照下会收缩。

paras.en: By directing light onto either fin, the researchers can trigger muscle contractions that make the fin flap and push the robot through water. Adjusting which fin receives light and how frequently it is illuminated allows the team to control both its speed and direction.
paras.zh: 通过将光照射到任一鳍上，研究人员可以触发肌肉收缩，使鳍拍打并将机器人推入水中。调整哪个鳍接收光线以及照亮的频率可以让团队控制其速度和方向。

paras.en: In experiments, the remarkably thin robot successfully swam and turned through a simple underwater maze. At maximum speed, it covered approximately four times its body length per minute. Although that is much slower than an Olympic swimmer, who can travel up to 65 body lengths per minute, it is comparable to the swimming pace of a cow shark moving leisurely through the ocean.
paras.zh: 在实验中，这个非常瘦的机器人成功地游泳并穿过一个简单的水下迷宫。在最大速度下，它每分钟行走的距离约为其身体长度的四倍。尽管这比奥运会游泳运动员每分钟游动 65 个身体长度要慢得多，但它的游泳速度与在海洋中悠闲游动的牛鲨的游泳速度相当。

paras.en: "It takes a lot of force to move through water versus air," says study author Ritu Raman, associate professor of mechanical engineering at MIT. "The robot's quite strong, given its size. "
paras.zh: 研究作者、麻省理工学院机械工程副教授 Ritu Raman 表示：“相对于空气来说，在水中移动需要很大的力。” “考虑到它的尺寸，这个机器人相当坚固。”

paras.en: A New Generation of Robots Powered by Living Muscle
paras.zh: 由活肌肉驱动的新一代机器人

paras.en: The device represents the first demonstration of a very thin, two-dimensional robot that can move from place to place using living muscle tissue.
paras.zh: 该设备首次展示了一种非常薄的二维机器人，它可以利用活体肌肉组织从一个地方移动到另一个地方。

paras.en: Most existing biohybrid robots rely on relatively large, three-dimensional structures made from laboratory-grown skeletal muscle. Producing these structures typically requires millions of cells. Raman explains that thinner designs could reduce manufacturing costs while potentially improving movement efficiency.
paras.zh: 大多数现有的生物混合机器人依赖于由实验室生长的骨骼肌制成的相对较大的三维结构。生产这些结构通常需要数百万个细胞。拉曼解释说，更薄的设计可以降低制造成本，同时有可能提高运动效率。

paras.en: "Currently, biohybrid robots from our group and others' are built from bulky, 3D chunks of lab-grown skeletal muscle that require millions of cells to fabricate," says Raman, who notes that thinner, less bulky designs such as the team's new bot could be cheaper to build and could move more efficiently. "We believe that biohybrid robots powered by living muscle could one day perform delicate jobs like exploring environments too fragile or unpredictable for conventional hardware, because living tissue is soft, responsive to its surroundings, and can heal itself."
paras.zh: Raman 表示：“目前，我们团队和其他团队的生物混合机器人是由实验室培育的笨重 3D 骨骼肌块构建而成，需要数百万个细胞才能制造出来。”他指出，更薄、体积更小的设计（例如该团队的新机器人）的制造成本可能会更低，并且移动效率更高。 “我们相信，由活体肌肉驱动的生物混合机器人有一天可以执行精细的工作，例如探索对于传统硬件来说过于脆弱或不可预测的环境，因为活体组织是柔软的，对周围环境有反应，并且可以自我修复。”

paras.en: The MIT research team also included first author Maheera Bawa, along with Arielle Berman, Laura Schwendeman, Ferdows Afghah, and Seanbiron Johnson.
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院的研究团队还包括第一作者 Maheera Bawa、Arielle Berman、Laura Schwendeman、Ferdows Afghah 和 Seanbiron Johnson。

paras.en: From Artificial Muscle to a Swimming Robot
paras.zh: 从人造肌肉到游泳机器人

paras.en: The new swimming robot builds on an earlier achievement by Raman's laboratory. Last year, the researchers created an artificial muscle disk inspired by the human iris, demonstrating how a thin layer of living cells could produce precisely controlled movements.
paras.zh: 新型游泳机器人建立在拉曼实验室早期成果的基础上。去年，研究人员受人类虹膜的启发，创造了一种人造肌肉盘，展示了薄薄的一层活细胞如何产生精确控制的运动。

paras.en: For that project, the engineers patterned a gel disk with grooves extending outward from its center and forming concentric circles. They then placed living muscle cells on the surface, where the cells grew into a thin layer following the patterned channels.
paras.zh: 在该项目中，工程师们在凝胶盘上绘制了图案，凹槽从其中心向外延伸并形成同心圆。然后，他们将活体肌肉细胞放置在表面，细胞沿着图案通道生长成薄层。

paras.en: When illuminated, the muscle tissue contracted in different directions, causing the disk to stretch and compress. Its movements resembled the way the iris of the human eye changes shape as the pupil expands or narrows.
paras.zh: 当光照时，肌肉组织向不同方向收缩，导致椎间盘拉伸和压缩。它的运动类似于人眼虹膜随着瞳孔扩大或缩小而改变形状的方式。

paras.en: The experiment established that researchers could grow extremely thin muscle layers in intricate arrangements and use light to control their movements along multiple directions.
paras.zh: 该实验表明，研究人员可以以复杂的方式生长出极薄的肌肉层，并利用光来控制它们沿多个方向的运动。

paras.en: "People hadn't seen this muscle architecture engineered from scratch before," Raman says. "And the cells were moving in multiple directions. But they only moved about 100 microns. From a robotics perspective, their movements were tiny."
paras.zh: “人们以前从未见过这种从头开始设计的肌肉结构，”拉曼说。 “细胞向多个方向移动。但它们只移动了大约 100 微米。从机器人的角度来看，它们的移动很小。”

paras.en: For the latest project, the researchers wanted to dramatically increase the amount of movement and force generated by the muscle cells. Their goal was to produce contractions powerful enough to propel a robot through water.
paras.zh: 对于最新的项目，研究人员希望大幅增加肌肉细胞产生的运动量和力量。他们的目标是产生足够强大的收缩来推动机器人在水中前进。

paras.en: They determined that achieving this would require a better foundation for the living muscle tissue.
paras.zh: 他们确定，实现这一目标需要为活体肌肉组织提供更好的基础。

paras.en: The earlier artificial iris had used fibrin, an exceptionally soft gel, as its underlying structure. However, the team found that fibrin could quickly shrink under the forces exerted by contracting muscle cells, limiting the effectiveness of the resulting movement.
paras.zh: 早期的人造虹膜使用纤维蛋白（一种非常柔软的凝胶）作为其基础结构。然而，研究小组发现，纤维蛋白在收缩肌肉细胞所施加的力的作用下会迅速收缩，从而限制了由此产生的运动的有效性。

paras.en: To overcome this problem, the engineers investigated three characteristics of the gel foundation: its chemical composition, its stiffness, and the dimensions and geometry of the grooves used to organize muscle growth.
paras.zh: 为了克服这个问题，工程师们研究了凝胶粉底的三个特性：其化学成分、硬度以及用于组织肌肉生长的凹槽的尺寸和几何形状。

paras.en: "For engineering any type of tissue, it's known that these are knobs you can tune," Raman says. "And we wanted to optimize all these parameters to support live muscle cells."
paras.zh: “对于任何类型的组织的工程设计，众所周知，这些都是可以调节的旋钮，”拉曼说。 “我们希望优化所有这些参数以支持活肌肉细胞。”

paras.en: Engineering a Stronger Muscle-Powered Robot
paras.zh: 设计更强大的肌肉驱动机器人

paras.en: Finding the right supporting material required testing gels with different formulations, stiffness levels, and surface patterns.
paras.zh: 找到合适的支撑材料需要测试具有不同配方、硬度水平和表面图案的凝胶。

paras.en: The researchers compared several groove shapes, including narrow channels with square profiles and longer channels with curved bottoms. They discovered that muscle cells aligned more effectively inside square-shaped grooves.
paras.zh: 研究人员比较了几种凹槽形状，包括具有方形轮廓的窄通道和具有弯曲底部的较长通道。他们发现肌肉细胞在方形凹槽内排列更有效。

paras.en: This alignment was important because muscle cells that grow in the same direction are more likely to merge into fibers. Those fibers can then form stronger muscle tissue that contracts in a coordinated way. The square grooves therefore provided a more effective structure for producing force.
paras.zh: 这种排列很重要，因为朝同一方向生长的肌肉细胞更有可能合并成纤维。然后，这些纤维可以形成更强大的肌肉组织，以协调的方式收缩。因此，方形凹槽提供了更有效的产生力的结构。

paras.en: The team also replaced fibrin with gelatin methacrylate (GelMA), a material commonly used to grow and engineer biological tissue.
paras.zh: 该团队还用甲基丙烯酸明胶（GelMA）取代了纤维蛋白，这是一种常用于生长和改造生物组织的材料。

paras.en: By adjusting the formulation of GelMA, the researchers produced supporting gels with varying degrees of stiffness. They then examined how muscle cells developed on each surface and measured their ability to generate force.
paras.zh: 通过调整 GelMA 的配方，研究人员生产出了不同硬度的支撑凝胶。然后，他们检查了肌肉细胞在每个表面上的发育情况，并测量了它们产生力量的能力。

paras.en: Stiffer gels produced the best results. On these firmer surfaces, muscle cells grew in better alignment and generated stronger contractions.
paras.zh: 较硬的凝胶产生最佳效果。在这些更坚硬的表面上，肌肉细胞生长得更好，并产生更强的收缩。

paras.en: The engineers next investigated how thick the gel should be. They determined that a film measuring approximately half a millimeter offered an effective balance. It was sturdy enough to support a single layer of muscle cells while remaining sufficiently lightweight to prevent the contracting cells from detaching from the surface.
paras.zh: 工程师接下来研究了凝胶的厚度。他们确定大约半毫米的薄膜可以提供有效的平衡。它足够坚固，可以支撑单层肌肉细胞，同时保持足够轻的重量，以防止收缩细胞从表面脱落。

paras.en: The team further improved muscle performance through a form of exercise. Repeated pulses of light stimulated the cells to contract, strengthening the muscle tissue before it was incorporated into the swimming robot.
paras.zh: 该团队通过某种形式的锻炼进一步提高了肌肉性能。重复的光脉冲刺激细胞收缩，增强肌肉组织，然后将其纳入游泳机器人中。

paras.en: With the gel structure optimized and the muscle cells strengthened, the researchers assembled their swimming device.
paras.zh: 随着凝胶结构的优化和肌肉细胞的强化，研究人员组装了他们的游泳装置。

paras.en: The finished robot consisted of a thin gel framework divided into two fins. Both sides of the gel were patterned with square-bottomed grooves and covered with living muscle cells. As the cells developed, they fused into organized muscle fibers capable of contracting together.
paras.zh: 完成的机器人由一个薄的凝胶框架组成，分为两个鳍。凝胶的两侧均刻有方底凹槽图案，并覆盖有活体肌肉细胞。随着细胞的发育，它们融合成能够收缩在一起的有组织的肌纤维。

paras.en: Each fin could be activated independently using light, giving the researchers a simple way to control the robot's movements.
paras.zh: 每个鳍都可以用光独立激活，为研究人员提供了一种控制机器人运动的简单方法。

paras.en: "You can think of the robot as having two independent muscles," Raman says. "If we shine a light on just one, only that muscle moves. If shining on both, they both flap."
paras.zh: “你可以把机器人想象成有两块独立的肌肉，”拉曼说。 “如果我们只用灯光照射其中一个，则只有该肌肉会移动。如果同时照射到两者，它们都会拍动。”

paras.en: To test the device, the researchers placed it inside a large petri dish filled with water. They then moved a light source by hand, illuminating the fins to guide the robot through a maze positioned inside the dish.
paras.zh: 为了测试该设备，研究人员将其放入一个装满水的大培养皿中。然后，他们用手移动光源，照亮鳍，引导机器人穿过位于盘子内的迷宫。

paras.en: As the muscles contracted, the fins flapped and propelled the robot through the water. By changing the light stimulation, the engineers successfully controlled its movement and helped it navigate the obstacles.
paras.zh: 当肌肉收缩时，鳍拍打并推动机器人在水中前进。通过改变光刺激，工程师成功地控制了它的运动并帮助它穿越障碍物。

paras.en: Although the robot demonstrated the ability to swim and steer, its current shape remains relatively simple. The primary objective of the experiment was to establish that an exceptionally thin layer of engineered muscle tissue could generate enough force for swimming.
paras.zh: 尽管该机器人展示了游泳和驾驶的能力，但其目前的形状仍然相对简单。该实验的主要目的是确定一层特别薄的工程肌肉组织可以产生足够的游泳力。

paras.en: The researchers now plan to refine the robot's body to improve its speed. Beyond demonstrating a new approach to biohybrid robotics, the technology could eventually be useful for monitoring aquatic environments or operating in locations where conventional rigid machines might cause damage.
paras.zh: 研究人员现在计划改进机器人的身体以提高其速度。除了展示生物混合机器人的新方法之外，该技术最终还可用于监测水生环境或在传统刚性机器可能造成损坏的地方进行操作。

paras.en: "Our next goal is to optimize the body design to enable faster swimming," Raman says. "But even at slow swim speeds, one could imagine a muscle-powered swimmer being used for purposes like environmental monitoring in aquatic environments."
paras.zh: “我们的下一个目标是优化身体设计，以实现更快的游泳，”拉曼说。 “但即使游泳速度较慢，人们也可以想象一名肌肉驱动的游泳者被用于水生环境中的环境监测等目的。”

paras.en: The Office of Naval Research provided partial funding for this research.
paras.zh: 海军研究办公室为这项研究提供了部分资金。

paras.en: Materials provided by Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Original written by Jennifer Chu. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由麻省理工学院提供。原创作者：朱珍妮。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。

paras.en: - Maheera Bawa, Arielle Berman, Laura Schwendeman, Ferdows Afghah, Seanbiron Johnson, Ritu Raman. 2D Skeletal Muscle Thin Film Actuators Enhance Efficiency of Biohybrid Robots. Advanced Functional Materials, 2026; DOI: 10.1002/adfm.78065
paras.zh: - Maheera Bawa、Arielle Berman、Laura Schwendeman、Ferdows Afghah、Seanbiron Johnson、Ritu Raman。 2D 骨骼肌薄膜执行器提高生物混合机器人的效率。先进功能材料，2026； DOI：10.1002/adfm.78065

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

paras.en: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station.
paras.zh: 2007年10月23日，发现号航天飞机将和谐舱发射到国际空间站。

paras.en: The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts.
paras.zh: Harmony 模块是一个公用设施枢纽，宽 14 英尺，长 24 英尺，大约有一辆小巴的长度。它与欧洲航天局的哥伦布舱和日本的 Kibo 实验室一起，作为美国宇航员的船员宿舍。

paras.en: Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station, they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node.
paras.zh: 安装完成后，空间站的大小从三居室房屋大小变成了五居室房屋大小。当宇航员将 Harmony 运送到空间站时，他们将其暂时连接到 Unity 节点。

paras.en: After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module. This made room for Harmony to then dock at its permanent home next to the Destiny module.
paras.zh: 航天飞机离开后，宇航员使用空间站的机械臂将航天飞机对接端口移至命运舱。这为 Harmony 腾出了空间，让其可以停靠在命运模块旁边的永久位置。

paras.en: In 2007, the International Space Station was much smaller than it is today in terms of living space for its astronaut crew. The Harmony connecting module changed all that.
paras.zh: 2007年，国际空间站宇航员的居住空间比现在小得多。 Harmony 连接模块改变了这一切。

paras.en: The STS-120 mission opened a new phase of ISS expansion by adding a vital connecting hub for future modules. Prior to Harmony's launch, the last new room addition to the ISS had occurred in 2001, when Russia's Pirs docking module (since discarded) arrived.
paras.zh: STS-120 任务为未来模块添加了重要的连接枢纽，开启了国际空间站扩展的新阶段。在 Harmony 发射之前，国际空间站最后一次添加新房间是在 2001 年，当时俄罗斯的 Pirs 对接模块（现已废弃）抵达。

paras.en: The Harmony module (its original name was Node 2), was the second NASA-led hub module (after the Unity, or Node 1, module) for the ISS. It was built for NASA by the Italy-based Thales Alenia Space and is covered with five "common berthing mechanisms," or connecting points for different ISS modules.
paras.zh: Harmony 模块（原名 Node 2）是 NASA 领导的第二个国际空间站枢纽模块（继 Unity 或 Node 1 模块之后）。它是由意大利泰雷兹阿莱尼亚航天公司为美国宇航局建造的，覆盖有五个“通用停泊机制”，或不同国际空间站模块的连接点。

paras.en: After the two-week STS-120 flight, Harmony was moved from a temporary berth at the Unity module to the forward port on the NASA's main Destiny laboratory. Once there, it served as a connection point for Europe's Columbus lab on the starboard side, and Japan's massive Kibo lab on the port side. Some of its ports have been used by visiting caargo ships and a docking port on its roof allows visiting vehicles to park there.
paras.zh: 经过两周的 STS-120 飞行后，Harmony 号从 Unity 模块的临时停泊处移至 NASA 主要命运实验室的前港。到达那里后，它成为右舷欧洲哥伦布实验室和左舷日本大型基博实验室的连接点。它的一些港口已被来访的货运船使用，其屋顶上的停靠端口允许来访的车辆停泊在那里。

paras.en: Inside the module are eight payload racks that include four used for avionics and four others for either stowage or crew quarters. NASA's astronaut crew quarters are based in the Harmony module. The name Harmony was selected durng a public naming contest by NASA.
paras.zh: 模块内部有八个有效载荷架，其中四个用于航空电子设备，另外四个用于装载或机组人员宿舍。美国宇航局的宇航员宿舍位于和谐舱内。 Harmony 这个名字是在 NASA 的公开命名竞赛中选出的。

paras.en: Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
paras.zh: 想要更多太空历史吗？查看我们完整的“太空中的这一天”故事存档，并在 YouTube 上观看“太空中的这一天”视频。

paras.en: Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.
paras.zh: Hanneke Weitering 是西北太平洋地区的一名多媒体记者，在 FutureFlight.aero 和 Aviation International News 报道航空业的未来，此前曾担任 Space.com 的航天和天文学新闻编辑。作为一名拥有 10 多年科学新闻经验的编辑，她曾为学术课堂杂志、MedPage Today 和橡树岭国家实验室计算科学研究所撰写文章。在家乡诺克斯维尔的田纳西大学学习物理学后，她在纽约大学获得了科学、健康和环境报告 (SHERP) 研究生学位。 Hanneke 于 2016 年加入 Space.com 团队，担任专职撰稿人和制作人，涵盖航天和天文学等主题。她目前与她的猫和两条蛇住在太空针塔所在地西雅图。在业余时间，汉内克喜欢探索落基山脉，沐浴在大自然中，寻找黑暗的天空凝视宇宙。
