It is the first DC Studios title to launch since Supergirl faced box office headwinds over the summer.
paras.zh: 华纳兄弟公司于周五在北美 3,400 多家影院上映了《泥面》，这部由 DC 工作室制作的人体恐怖电影在周四的预映中获得了 350 万美元的收入。该工作室预计预算为 4,400 万美元的《粘土面》的国内首映票房为 2,500 万至 3,000 万美元，国际票房为 2,000 万至 2,500 万美元。这是自《超女》夏季遭遇票房逆风以来，DC 工作室推出的第一款作品。

paras.en: Tom Rhys Harries and Naomi Ackie star in the story of Matt Hagen (Harries), an actor who turns to a scientist (Ackie) for assistance when his face becomes disfigured. In his review for The Hollywood Reporter, critic Frank Scheck called Clayface “a big swing that definitely pays off.”
paras.zh: 汤姆·里斯·哈里斯 (Tom Rhys Harries) 和娜奥米·阿基 (Naomi Ackie) 主演了演员马特·哈根 (哈里斯饰) 的故事，当他的脸毁容时，他向科学家 (阿基饰) 寻求帮助。评论家 Frank Scheck 在《好莱坞报道》的评论中称《Clayface》是“一次绝对有回报的重大转变”。

paras.en: You Can See Everything added $2.2 million on Thursday from 855 North American locations to bring its domestic cume to $25.6 million. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim‘s documentary about disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes widens to 2,600 theaters domestically on Friday for its sophomore frame. Its $15 million opening marked the highest-grossing launch for a release under 1,000 theaters since 2006’s Borat.
paras.zh: 《You Can See Everything》周四在北美 855 个地点增加了 220 万美元，使其国内收入达到 2,560 万美元。内森·菲尔德 (Nathan Fielder) 和兰斯·奥本海姆 (Lance Oppenheim) 拍摄的关于失宠的希拉洛斯 (Theranos) 创始人伊丽莎白·霍姆斯 (Elizabeth Holmes) 的纪录片周五在国内 2,600 家影院上映，第二季上映。该片首映票房 1,500 万美元，创下自 2006 年的《波拉特》以来在 1,000 家影院上映的票房最高的影片。

paras.en: Wicker lands in 1,471 North American theaters from Black Bear, grossing $620,000 in Thursday previews for directors Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer’s romantic fantasy that premiered at Sundance. Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård star in the movie about a woman in a quiet village who gets a wicker husband. In his review for THR, critic Richard Lawson praised Wicker’s “winning mix of irreverence and compassion.”
paras.zh: 由黑熊执导的《威克》登陆北美 1,471 家影院，周四在圣丹斯电影节首映的导演埃莉诺·威尔逊和亚历克斯·休斯顿·费舍尔的浪漫奇幻片中获得了 62 万美元的票房。奥利维亚·科尔曼和亚历山大·斯卡斯加德主演的这部电影讲述了一个安静村庄里的女人嫁给了一个柳条丈夫的故事。评论家理查德·劳森在《THR》的评论中称赞威克“将不敬和同情心完美结合”。

paras.en: Klara and the Sun collected $85,000 from Thursday previews for the Sony Pictures release that stars Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams. Hailing from 3000 Pictures and Spyglass Media Group, director Taika Waititi’s feature adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s novel hits 850 theaters Friday and follows a robot companion connecting with a sick girl. THR chief film critic David Rooney deemed it a “wretched mess.”
paras.zh: 克拉拉和太阳报在周四索尼影业发行的由珍娜·奥尔特加和艾米·亚当斯主演的预告片中筹集了 85,000 美元。由 3000 Pictures 和 Spyglass Media Group 出品的导演塔伊卡·维迪提 (Taika Waititi) 改编自石黑一雄小说的故事片周五在 850 家影院上映，讲述了机器人伴侣与生病女孩的故事。 《好莱坞报道》首席影评人大卫·鲁尼认为这是“一团糟”。

paras.en: Also opening this weekend are Laika’s stop-motion animated feature Wildwood, with director Travis Knight’s film screening in 2,926 domestic theaters, and Amazon MGM Studios’ Sacha Baron Cohen-led comedy Ali G: Who Iz I?, which hits just 125 North American locations for one week only.
paras.zh: 本周末上映的还有莱卡 (Laika) 的定格动画长片《怀尔德伍德》(Wildwood)，导演特拉维斯·奈特 (Travis Knight) 的电影在 2,926 家国内影院放映；亚马逊米高梅影业 (Amazon MGM Studios) 的萨莎·拜伦·科恩 (Sacha Baron Cohen) 主演的喜剧《阿里·G：我是谁？》(Ali G: Who Iz I?) 仅在北美 125 个地点上映一周。

articles.title: Fox News May Be More Disruption-Proof Than Ever
articles.author: Alex Weprin

paras.en: On Oct. 6, Fox News Media CEO Suzanne Scott gathered with her senior leadership team and some Fox News originals like Steve Doocy, Brit Hume and Trace Gallagher in Nasdaq’s Studio A, right in the middle of Times Square, to ring the closing bell.
paras.zh: 10 月 6 日，福克斯新闻媒体首席执行官苏珊娜·斯科特 (Suzanne Scott) 与她的高级领导团队以及史蒂夫·杜西 (Steve Doocy)、布里特·休姆 (Brit Hume) 和特雷斯·加拉格尔 (Trace Gallagher) 等福克斯新闻原创人士聚集在位于时代广场中心的纳斯达克 A 工作室，敲响了收盘钟。

paras.en: A few minutes before she rang the bell, Scott took to the podium to deliver remarks celebrating Fox News Channel’s 30th anniversary, recognizing a media platform that transformed not only the cable news landscape, but the political landscape as well.
paras.zh: 在按铃前几分钟，斯科特走上讲台发表讲话，庆祝福克斯新闻频道成立 30 周年，承认这个媒体平台不仅改变了有线新闻格局，还改变了政治格局。

paras.en: “As we celebrate 30 years of stories reported and analyzed, and history witnessed at each turn, we also look ahead because the next chapter of media is being shaped right now by new technology, new platforms, and new ways of connecting with audiences,” the CEO added.
paras.zh: 这位首席执行官补充道：“当我们庆祝 30 年来报道和分析的故事以及每一个转折点见证的历史时，我们也展望未来，因为新技术、新平台和与受众联系的新方式正在塑造媒体的下一个篇章。”

paras.en: Fox News is a powerful force in American politics and culture, and a dominant one at that. It decimates the cable news competition in the ratings (it now tops CNN and MS NOW combined handily), and over the last year has had its sights set on the broadcast networks.
paras.zh: 福克斯新闻是美国政治和文化中的一股强大力量，而且是主导力量。它在收视率方面击败了有线电视新闻竞争者（现在它轻而易举地超过了 CNN 和 MS NOW 的总和），并在去年将目光投向了广播网络。

paras.en: And an interview on the channel can still make or break powerful figures. Just look at Katie Zacharia.
paras.zh: 频道上的采访仍然可以成就或毁掉有权有势的人物。看看凯蒂·撒迦利亚就知道了。

paras.en: The newly-minted White House press secretary was facing a barrage of criticism over her first press conference earlier this month, and questions over whether she was really a working lawyer.
paras.zh: 这位新上任的白宫新闻秘书在本月早些时候的第一次新闻发布会上面临着一系列批评，并质疑她是否真的是一名在职律师。

paras.en: But it was a Sean Hannity interview that was the final straw, with the Fox News host interrogating her about the criticisms and her past statements. The next morning, the White House said that she would be exiting the role after only five days on the job, with some pundits comparing her appearance on Hannity to a mob hit.
paras.zh: 但肖恩·汉尼提的采访成为了最后一根稻草，福克斯新闻主持人就这些批评和她过去的言论对她进行了审讯。第二天早上，白宫表示，她将在上任仅五天后退出该职位，一些专家将她在《汉尼提》中的亮相比作暴徒袭击。

paras.en: Hannity, for his part, tells The Hollywood Reporter that he wasn’t a hitman, he was just doing his job.
paras.zh: 汉尼蒂则告诉《好莱坞报道》，他不是杀手，他只是在做他的工作。

paras.en: “My audience knows exactly where I stand, but that doesn’t mean I’m not going to ask tough questions when they’re warranted,” he says, adding: “I gave her the opportunity to tell her side of the story and let the audience judge for themselves. I assumed she would take advantage of the opportunity and put all of this to rest before the next briefing.”
paras.zh: “我的观众确切地知道我的立场，但这并不意味着我不会在有必要的时候提出尖锐的问题，”他说，并补充道：“我给了她机会讲述她的故事，并让观众自己判断。我以为她会利用这个机会，在下一次简报之前把这一切都抛诸脑后。”

paras.en: Hannity notes, “I’ve been doing this long enough to know that people will have strong reactions. My job is to ask the questions, get answers and let the audience decide for themselves. I allowed her a lot of time uninterrupted for her to answer.”
paras.zh: 汉尼蒂指出：“我已经这样做了足够长的时间，知道人们会有强烈的反应。我的工作是提出问题，获得答案，然后让观众自己决定。我给了她很多不受打扰的时间来回答。”

paras.en: The power of the Fox News platform at work. It can make a political career, or it can break it.
paras.zh: 福克斯新闻平台的力量正在发挥作用。它可以成就一个政治生涯，也可以毁掉它。

paras.en: When it launched 30 years ago however it was a challenger brand, a disruptive bet made by Murdoch and Roger Ailes that there were Americans not being well-served by the status quo, CNN.
paras.zh: 然而，当它在 30 年前推出时，它是一个挑战者品牌，是默多克和罗杰·艾尔斯做出的颠覆性赌注，即美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的现状并未为美国人提供良好的服务。

paras.en: But what has many executives at its competitors especially jealous is that Fox News has also been pouring vastly more resources into digital, willing to disrupt itself … at least a little bit, even as CNN and MS NOW are only just now really investing in the space as they launch their own direct-to-consumer products, playing a game of catchup.
paras.zh: 但令其竞争对手的许多高管尤其嫉妒的是，福克斯新闻也在数字领域投入了大量资源，愿意自我颠覆……至少有一点点，尽管 CNN 和 MS NOW 刚刚真正投资该领域，推出了自己的直接面向消费者的产品，玩着追赶游戏。

paras.en: “We still feel like an upstart. It’s very interesting to be 30 years in, and still feel like you’re the challenger,” says Dana Perino, the longtime host of America’s Newsroom and The Five. “We are number one, but they still love to put us down. It’s pretty funny. You look at the ratings across the board. I mean, we’re number one all the time, and I think there’s probably grudging admiration for Fox.”
paras.zh: “我们仍然感觉自己像个暴发户。30 年后，仍然感觉自己是挑战者，这非常有趣，”《美国新闻编辑室》和《五人组》的长期主持人达纳·佩里诺 (Dana Perino) 说道。 “我们是第一，但他们仍然喜欢贬低我们。这很有趣。你看看全面的收视率。我的意思是，我们一直是第一，我认为人们可能对福克斯有勉强的钦佩。”

paras.en: Hannity, who was there on day one, was more blunt (as he often is).
paras.zh: 汉尼蒂第一天就在场，他的态度更加直率（就像他经常做的那样）。

paras.en: “I think the story of Fox is going to be studied for decades and decades to come,” he says. “Honestly, what it’s been able to accomplish as a channel, I think it has become the most impactful channel that’s available politically and newsworthy-wise, and it’s a vision that did fill a void and is still filling a void, I would argue.”
paras.zh: “我认为福克斯的故事将在未来几十年内得到研究，”他说。 “老实说，它作为一个频道所取得的成就，我认为它已经成为在政治和新闻价值方面最具影响力的频道，我认为，这个愿景确实填补了空白，并且仍在填补空白。”

paras.en: Now, Rupert Murdoch views Fox as a core part of his legacy, as last year’s family trust battle underscores, with his son Lachlan ultimately securing control of the empire after battling (and ultimately settling with) his siblings.
paras.zh: 现在，鲁珀特·默多克将福克斯视为他遗产的核心部分，正如去年的家族信托之争所强调的那样，他的儿子拉克兰在与他的兄弟姐妹斗争（并最终和解）后最终获得了对帝国的控制权。

paras.en: “It would be a disaster for at least the US and Australia if these assets fell into the wrong hands,” Rupert Murdoch said in testimony released as part of the hearings, adding that Fox News and his other media brands provided an “alternative voice” and were “essential for democracies.”
paras.zh: 鲁珀特·默多克在听证会发布的证词中表示：“如果这些资产落入坏人之手，至少对美国和澳大利亚来说将是一场灾难。”他补充说，福克斯新闻和他的其他媒体品牌提供了“另类声音”，并且“对民主国家至关重要”。

paras.en: From a challenger brand to being essential for democracies is no small jump.
paras.zh: 从挑战者品牌到民主国家不可或缺的品牌是一个不小的飞跃。

paras.en: At the core of Fox’s operations is the relentless focus on the viewers. A veteran CNN executive once told me that at CNN, the news was the star, which explained why when something big was happening, TV sets across the world would be tuned to those three red letters.
paras.zh: 福克斯运营的核心是对观众的不懈关注。 CNN 的一位资深高管曾经告诉我，在 CNN，新闻就是明星，这解释了为什么当有大事发生时，世界各地的电视机都会调到这三个红色字母。

paras.en: At Fox, the viewer is the star, or at least the north star, the thing that everyone is chasing.
paras.zh: 在福克斯，观众就是星星，或者至少是北极星，是每个人都在追逐的东西。

paras.en: Hannity describes Fox like a pyramid. At other media companies, he argues, some CEO or editor-in-chief is at the top, dictating the vision to those below them (see CBS News and Bari Weiss). It’s a structure that many outside Fox project on the media company. Hannity, however, doesn’t see it like that. He describes an operation where the executives, and even the Murdochs, are at the bottom of the pyramid.
paras.zh: 汉尼蒂将福克斯描述为一座金字塔。他认为，在其他媒体公司，一些首席执行官或主编处于最高层，向下面的人传达愿景（参见哥伦比亚广播公司新闻和巴里韦斯）。这是福克斯以外的许多人为这家媒体公司所设想的结构。然而，汉尼蒂却不这么认为。他描述了这样一种运作方式：高管们，甚至默多克家族，都处于金字塔的最底层。

paras.en: “At the top of the triangle in my world is the viewer, they are the most important person in our orbit because if we’re not serving them, then we’re failing,” he says. “Below the viewer would be the host because they have the closest relationship with the viewer. Below them are all these hardworking producers and tech people and researchers and writers, and all these people that help put a show together.
paras.zh: “在我的世界中，三角形的顶部是观众，他们是我们轨道上最重要的人，因为如果我们不为他们服务，那么我们就失败了，”他说。 “观众下面是主持人，因为他们与观众的关系最密切。在他们下面是所有这些辛勤工作的制片人、技术人员、研究人员和作家，以及所有帮助制作节目的人。

paras.en: “And at the bottom of the triangle, the base of that triangle — and this is how it’s always kind of worked for me — are people like you mentioned: Rupert, Lachlan, Suzanne Scott,” he continued. “They are a support pushing up not just the vision, but they’re helping me to get that viewer. And by offering that base of support, it makes me better, and makes me want to be better at what I do to help achieve the goal of satisfying the viewers that are watching.”
paras.zh: “在三角形的底部，三角形的底部 - 这就是它总是对我起作用的方式 - 是像你提到的那样的人：鲁珀特，拉克兰，苏珊娜·斯科特，”他继续说道。 “他们不仅是提升愿景的支持，而且还帮助我吸引观众。通过提供这种支持基础，它让我变得更好，让我想要做得更好，帮助实现满足正在观看的观众的目标。”

paras.en: What makes for Fox News’ secret sauce is a little harder to formulate. Sure, it has plenty of conservative and right-of-center voices, especially in primetime, but there are plenty of others that do that too.
paras.zh: 福克斯新闻的秘诀有点难以表述。当然，它有很多保守派和中右翼的声音，尤其是在黄金时段，但还有很多其他人也这样做。

paras.en: Hannity recalls a scene from the film Private Parts, where Howard Stern is introduced to the audience with the “radio voice” that was once a dime a dozen on local stations across America. Hannity, doing an impression of Stern in the movie, says he relates to the scene and to the shock jock’s plight in the film (“although I would argue he’s gotten a little too woke for everybody I know,” he quips).
paras.zh: 汉尼蒂回忆起电影《私处》中的一个场景，霍华德·斯特恩向观众介绍了曾经在美国各地电台中随处可见的“广播声音”。汉尼蒂在电影中模仿了斯特恩，他说他对电影中的场景和震惊运动员的困境很感兴趣（“尽管我认为他对我认识的每个人来说都有点太清醒了，”他打趣道）。

paras.en: “When [Stern] became his unique self, when [Don] Imus became his unique self, when Rush [Limbaugh] became his unique self, when [Bill] O’Reilly was his unique self, and then you go all the way up to the lineup all throughout Fox … once you become your authentic self, I think that’s when you can do your best work,” Hannity says in explaining the channel’s approach to opinion programming.
paras.zh: “当[斯特恩]成为他独特的自我，当[唐]伊穆斯成为他独特的自我，当拉什[林堡]成为他独特的自我，当[比尔]奥莱利成为他独特的自我，然后你一路上升到整个福克斯的阵容......一旦你成为真实的自我，我认为那就是你可以做得最好的时候，”汉尼蒂在解释该频道的观点节目制作方法时说道。

paras.en: Any conversation with Fox News on-air talent will inevitably include them noting that no one tells them what to say, they are expressing themselves fully.
paras.zh: 与福克斯新闻播音员的任何对话都不可避免地会让他们注意到没有人告诉他们该说什么，他们正在充分表达自己。

paras.en: “We are so protected that we have confidence to be able to say whatever we think, and know that as long as we’re being honest and truthful, and coming from a good place, we’re going to get back up here,” says Perino. “I’ve never worked anywhere else. I don’t know if that’s true in other places, but our corporate culture here is really good. In fact, I don’t think it’s ever been better.”
paras.zh: 佩里诺说：“我们受到如此大的保护，我们有信心能够说出自己的想法，并且知道，只要我们诚实、诚实，并且来自一个好地方，我们就会回到这里。” “我从来没有在其他地方工作过。我不知道其他地方是否也是如此，但我们这里的企业文化真的很好。事实上，我认为没有比这更好的了。”

paras.en: To hear Fox News talent explain it, the on-air success is a combination of the editorial voice that encompasses its news and opinion programming, as well as the on-air product itself. For what its worth, executives at competing TV news organizations agree that Fox’s on-air polish is a big part of its success.
paras.zh: 据福克斯新闻人才解释，直播的成功是包含其新闻和观点节目的社论声音以及直播产品本身的结合。就其价值而言，竞争对手电视新闻机构的高管们一致认为，福克斯的广播精良是其成功的重要组成部分。

paras.en: “I like the pacing of news that Fox has,” says Hannity. “It moves from story to story to story, rather than getting you know caught up in a long NPR boring-ish delivery, which just doesn’t capture my interest.”
paras.zh: “我喜欢福克斯的新闻节奏，”汉尼蒂说。 “它从一个故事转移到另一个故事，而不是让你知道陷入冗长的 NPR 无聊的报道中，这根本无法引起我的兴趣。”

paras.en: “There is a quality to the aesthetic that is pleasing to the eye, right?” adds Perino.
paras.zh: “审美中有一种令人赏心悦目的品质，对吧？”佩里诺补充道。

paras.en: But the editorial approach of Fox News remains underappreciated. The central premise of Rupert’s gambit 30 years ago was that the elite news media in New York and Washington D.C. were not delivering all the news and opinions that were resonant in communities outside of the coasts. The company still operates within that rubric.
paras.zh: 但福克斯新闻的社论方法仍然没有得到足够的重视。鲁珀特 30 年前策略的核心前提是，纽约和华盛顿特区的精英新闻媒体并没有提供在沿海以外的社区引起共鸣的所有新闻和观点。该公司仍然按照该规则运营。

paras.en: “I think it’s honestly our competitive nature, our mentality of we’re not the elites, we’re representing those people back home,” says Lawrence Jones, a co-host of Fox & Friends. “I’m always thinking, how does this impact Texas? How does this impact my people that I love? And then I think about the national implications. But I look at it from that lens because I gotta go back home. My house is still in Texas. I gotta go back home and face stuff.”
paras.zh: “老实说，我认为这是我们的竞争天性，我们的心态是，我们不是精英，我们代表的是家乡的那些人，”《福克斯与朋友》的联合主持人劳伦斯·琼斯说。 “我总是在想，这对德克萨斯州有什么影响？这对我所爱的人有什么影响？然后我会考虑对国家的影响。但我从这个角度来看这件事，因为我必须回家。我的房子还在德克萨斯州。我必须回家面对一些事情。”

paras.en: “So if I go and I take this position, when I get home and I’m going through the grocery store and I’m going through Walmart or Kroger or H-E-B, I’m trying to channel my inner Texas,” he adds. “That’s the worst thing could ever happen to me, is for someone to say ‘what happened to you, you represented me, and you abandoned me.’ So, I think many of us, from a certain degree, carry that type of mentality.”
paras.zh: “所以，如果我去采取这个立场，当我回家时，我会经过杂货店，我会经过沃尔玛或克罗格或 H-E-B，我正在努力引导我内心的德克萨斯州，”他补充道。 “这是发生在我身上最糟糕的事情，就是有人说‘你发生了什么事，你代表了我，你抛弃了我。’所以，我认为我们中的许多人，从某种程度上来说，都持有这种心态。”

paras.en: That part of the conversation is reflected in Fox’s opinion shows, but less appreciated is how it shows up in the choices made in Fox’s news programming.
paras.zh: 这部分对话反映在福克斯的观点节目中，但不太受重视的是它如何出现在福克斯新闻节目的选择中。

paras.en: Fox executives would tell you that, while they may not have the vast global resources of a CNN, they still pour real money into news, with correspondents stationed around the U.S. and the world ready to spring into action when reality dictates it. Just look at Trey Yingst’s coverage of the aftermath of the attempted hijacking of the flight from the UAE to Israel last month, or its coverage of the L.A. wildfires last year led by Bill Melugin.
paras.zh: 福克斯高管会告诉你，虽然他们可能没有CNN那样庞大的全球资源，但他们仍然将真正的资金投入到新闻中，驻扎在美国和世界各地的记者随时准备在现实要求时采取行动。看看特雷·英斯特（ Trey Yingst ）对上个月从阿联酋飞往以色列的航班被劫持的后果的报道，或者其对去年由比尔·梅卢金（ Bill Melugin ）领导的洛杉矶野火的报道。

paras.en: But regular viewers of Fox’s news programs will also notice that, on days where there isn’t that obvious global story, they are happy to have pundits on to talk about the news, often grilled by Fox anchors, and they have an appreciation for angles of approach that is nonetheless distinct from its competition.
paras.zh: 但福克斯新闻节目的常客也会注意到，在没有那么明显的全球故事的日子里，他们很高兴有专家来谈论新闻，经常受到福克斯主播的拷问，而且他们对与竞争对手不同的方法角度有鉴赏力。

paras.en: Perino, for example, notes the upcoming midterm elections, where Democrat James Talarico appears to be running ahead of Republican Ken Paxton, threatening to turn a deep red Senate seat blue.
paras.zh: 例如，佩里诺指出，即将举行的中期选举中，民主党人詹姆斯·塔拉里科（ James Talarico ）似乎领先于共和党人肯·帕克斯顿（ Ken Paxton ） ，威胁要把参议院的一个深红色席位变成蓝色。

paras.en: “But the same is also true in Minnesota, where Michelle Tafoya could actually win, the first Republican in 18 years to win in Minnesota,” Perino says. “Just maybe we should talk about that race too.”
paras.zh: “但明尼苏达州也是如此，米歇尔·塔福亚实际上可能获胜，她是 18 年来第一位在明尼苏达州获胜的共和党人，”佩里诺说。 “也许我们也应该谈谈那场比赛。”

paras.en: Jones, recalling a segment that he says defines that approach, noted a series he did for the morning show, where he visits barbershops across the country to talk politics.
paras.zh: 琼斯回忆起他所说的定义这种方法的一个片段，并指出他为早间节目制作的一系列节目，其中他参观了全国各地的理发店谈论政治。

paras.en: “I’ve always told people I learned how to do TV in the barbershop,” he says. “The barbershop in Black America is the center of the community, politics, culture. Every topic is debated while you’re getting your haircut. Older gentlemen, younger gentlemen, you spar back and forth. You learn how to refine your argument in the barbershop.
paras.zh: “我总是告诉人们我在理发店学会了如何做电视，”他说。 “美国黑人的理发店是社区、政治、文化的中心。在你理发的时候，每个话题都会被争论。年长的绅士、年轻的绅士，你来回争论。你在理发店学习如何完善你的论点。

paras.en: “I told the bosses a long time ago, if you really want to capture the community, you’ve got to go to the barbershop, that’s where the real political conversations and cultural topics are happening,” he adds. “So a couple years ago, during the election, I told the bosses this, and they were game. We went around the country, went to barbershops, started having conversations, and in my final barbershop in the Bronx, then former-President Donald Trump came to the barbershop and had a conversation with me, and for a network to put resources behind that showed that they cared about my vision, cared about my instincts, and saw how it could attract audiences. I mean, I’ve got to be honest, the barbershops we were going to were mostly Latin and Black. That is not what stereotypically you think of as Fox News. Yet it was a really successful series.”
paras.zh: “我很久以前就告诉老板们，如果你真的想占领社区，你就必须去理发店，那里才是真正的政治对话和文化话题发生的地方，”他补充道。 “所以几年前，在选举期间，我告诉老板们这一点，他们很感兴趣。我们走遍全国，去理发店，开始交谈，在布朗克斯我的最后一家理发店，当时的前总统唐纳德·特朗普来到理发店并与我交谈，一个网络在背后投入资源表明他们关心我的愿景，关心我的直觉，并了解它如何吸引观众。我的意思是，我必须成为老实说，我们要去的理发店主要是拉丁裔和黑人，这不是你所认为的福克斯新闻，但这是一个非常成功的系列。”

paras.en: But Fox’s news programming has also benefited tremendously from the fact that President Trump, and people that want to reach Trump, know he watches religiously. Corporate executives, people who hope to secure government jobs, and even cabinet secretaries all lobby to be booked, knowing that he may be watching.
paras.zh: 但福克斯的新闻节目也从特朗普总统和想要接触特朗普的人知道他虔诚地观看这一事实中受益匪浅。企业高管、希望获得政府职位的人，甚至内阁秘书都在游说，希望得到任命，因为他们知道他可能会在监视。

paras.en: As Zacharia’s performance on Hannity demonstrated however, those appearances also carry risk.
paras.zh: 然而，正如撒迦利亚在《汉尼提》中的表演所表明的那样，这些出场也存在风险。

paras.en: Bret Baier’s Special Report in particular has become a must-stop destination for international politicians and business leaders, as well as Democrats seeking to make inroads with Fox’s large audience.
paras.zh: 尤其是布雷特·拜尔的特别报告，已成为国际政治家和商界领袖以及寻求赢得福克斯大量观众的民主党人的必读目的地。

paras.en: In just the last few months Baier has scored interviews with Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Sylvester Stallone, Vice President Vance, and multiple cabinet officials, while his colleague Martha MacCallum has held newsmaking interviews with Michigan Democratic Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed and New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani.
paras.zh: 就在过去的几个月里，拜尔接受了亚马逊创始人杰夫·贝佐斯、伊朗外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇、北约秘书长马克·鲁特、西尔维斯特·史泰龙、副总统万斯和多名内阁官员的采访，而他的同事玛莎·麦卡勒姆则接受了密歇根州民主党参议员候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德和纽约市市长佐赫兰·马姆达尼的新闻采访。

paras.en: “How silly people sound when they act like ignoring Fox or ignoring conservative media is a viable path forward, especially for people that are trying to get folks to vote for them,” says Jessica Tarlov, the liberal co-host on The Five. “I do think that there are two schools of thought on how to show up in these environments for a Democrat. One, which is show up and take a big swing and get your viral clip, and I think that has a very short shelf life. You get a couple of days of a great news cycle churn, you fundraise a lot if it’s an elected, for instance.
paras.zh: “当人们表现得无视福克斯或无视保守派媒体时，听起来多么愚蠢，这是一条可行的前进道路，特别是对于那些试图让人们投票给他们的人来说，”五人党的自由派联合主持人杰西卡·塔洛夫说。 “我确实认为，对于民主党人如何在这些环境中露面，有两种思想流派。一种是出现并采取重大举措并获得病毒式剪辑，我认为它的保质期非常短。例如，如果是民选的，你会得到几天的重大新闻周期搅动，你会筹集很多资金。

paras.en: “But then what happens? You didn’t really advance any theory of the case that’s going to be resonant in a long term way,” she adds. “If you’re in a D+50 seat, I understand why that might be exciting to you, but the second approach, which I think is so much better, is to be able to get your clip, if that’s what you’re looking for, but also to dialogue with someone who thinks differently than you and model the fact that your ideas can take some pushback and to show your dexterity with it, and that’s why [Fox News regular] Pete Buttigieg is so good at it, right?”
paras.zh: “但是接下来会发生什么？你并没有真正提出任何会引起长期共鸣的案例理论，”她补充道。 “如果你坐在 D+50 席位上，我理解为什么这可能会让你感到兴奋，但第二种方法，我认为更好，是能够获得你的剪辑，如果这就是你想要的，而且还能与与你想法不同的人对话，并模拟你的想法可能会受到一些阻力的事实，并展示你的灵活性，这就是为什么 [福克斯新闻常客] 皮特·布蒂吉格 (Pete Buttigieg) 如此擅长，对吧？”

paras.en: Fox’s business is benefiting too. In August, Lachlan Murdoch revealed that Fox News Media had added more than 400 new advertisers in its last fiscal year, an astonishing number of brands that were new to its news platforms.
paras.zh: 福克斯的业务也受益匪浅。 8 月，拉克兰·默多克 (Lachlan Murdoch) 透露，福克斯新闻媒体 (Fox News Media) 在上一财年新增了 400 多家新广告商，其新闻平台上的新品牌数量惊人。

paras.en: Indeed, a media buying source says that for companies that have any business in front of the government, or that are hoping to persuade political leaders, Fox News has become a must buy, thanks in large part to the fact that Trump is known to watch at any hour of the day when he has free time.
paras.zh: 事实上，一位媒体购买消息人士表示，对于那些在政府面前有业务的公司，或者希望说服政治领导人的公司来说，福克斯新闻已经成为必须购买的内容，这在很大程度上要归功于特朗普在一天中的任何时间都有空闲时间观看的事实。

paras.en: Of course, Fox’s relationship to President Trump is more complicated than it may appear on the surface.
paras.zh: 当然，福克斯与特朗普总统的关系比表面上看起来更为复杂。

paras.en: On the one hand, Fox’s talent has served as a proving ground for government officials, with Secretary Pete Hegseth, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro, Secretary Sean Duffy and Ambassador Mike Huckabee all former Fox hosts (until Oct. 13 Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle was also in that group, until troubling reports appeared in The Wall Street Journal, which shares ownership with Fox). Trump’s daughter-in-law Lara Trump hosts a weekend show, and his former Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt recently joined as a contributor.
paras.zh: 一方面，福克斯的才华成为了政府官员的试验场，国务卿皮特·赫格斯 (Pete Hegseth)、美国检察官珍妮·皮罗 (Jeanine Pirro)、国务卿肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 和大使迈克·赫卡比 (Mike Huckabee) 都是福克斯的前主持人（直到 10 月 13 日，大使金伯利·吉尔福伊尔 (Kimberly Guilfoyle) 也在该组织中，直到与福克斯共享所有权的《华尔街日报》出现了令人不安的报道）。特朗普的儿媳劳拉·特朗普主持了一场周末秀，他的前新闻秘书卡罗琳·莱维特最近作为撰稿人加入。

paras.en: Trump has been a daily or weekly fixture of Fox News for about half its thirty years, the last 11 as President, former President or Presidential hopeful, and for years before that when he had a weekly call-in segment on the morning show and appeared frequently as a guest, segments that helped introduce him to that audience in a new way.
paras.zh: 特朗普在三十年的大约一半时间里一直是福克斯新闻的每日或每周固定节目，过去11年担任总统、前总统或总统候选人，在此之前的几年里，他每周都会在早间节目中接受电话采访，并经常作为嘉宾出现，这些片段帮助他以一种新的方式向观众介绍。

paras.en: Hannity says that before he ever ran for office, he would have late night calls with Trump, where they talked about policy and politics and other things that would ultimately become a core part of his political identity.
paras.zh: 汉尼蒂说，在他竞选公职之前，他会在深夜与特朗普通电话，他们谈论政策和政治以及其他最终将成为他政治身份核心部分的事情。

paras.en: “Those late night conversations convinced me,” Hannity recalls. “Not only was he conservative, but he was different, and he thought out of the box, and he was unique. And I realized at some point that he’s going to have an ability to connect in ways that no traditional politician would be able to connect.”
paras.zh: “那些深夜的谈话让我信服了，”汉尼蒂回忆道。 “他不仅保守，而且与众不同，他的思维跳出框框，而且他是独一无二的。我在某个时候意识到，他将有能力以传统政治家无法做到的方式建立联系。”

paras.en: On the other hand, Trump in recent weeks has lashed out at Fox for interviewing Democrats on its news programming, and lamented the channel giving Tarlov a seat at the table on The Five (never mind that the show’s format wouldn’t work without the token Democrat). He also complained about the channel not covering his rallies as aggressively as it had in the past. He is blunt about his view that he sees Fox as being part of his team, and views airtime for the opposition as not being congruent with that view.
paras.zh: 另一方面，特朗普最近几周猛烈抨击福克斯在其新闻节目中采访民主党人，并对该频道让塔尔洛夫在“五人组”的席位上感到遗憾（尽管如果没有象征性的民主党人，该节目的形式就无法运作）。他还抱怨该频道没有像过去那样积极报道他的集会。他直言不讳地表示，他认为福克斯是他团队的一部分，并且认为反对派的播出时间与他的观点不一致。

paras.en: Yet, he still has a strong relationship with many at Fox News. Baier is an occasional golf partner, and Hannity makes no secret of the fact that they are still personal friends, though he takes pains to note that he tries to separate their friendship from his day job.
paras.zh: 然而，他仍然与福克斯新闻的许多人保持着牢固的关系。拜尔偶尔会成为高尔夫球伙伴，汉尼蒂毫不掩饰他们仍然是私人朋友的事实，尽管他煞费苦心地指出，他试图将他们的友谊与他的日常工作分开。

paras.en: “I don’t think most people really understand him, which is frustrating to me,” Hannity says, adding that he makes an effort to split that personal relationship from what he says on his show. “I do make it a point of not hanging out with him. He invites me to stay [at Mar-a-Lago]. I don’t go very often, and it’s because if we’re talking as friends, I want to be as blunt and honest as I can be. And if we’re doing it professionally, I just need to be able to ask whatever I need to ask him. Period. Nothing. No holds barred.
paras.zh: 汉尼蒂说：“我认为大多数人并不真正理解他，这让我感到沮丧。”他补充说，他努力将这种个人关系与他在节目中所说的话分开。 “我确实不和他一起出去玩。他邀请我留在[海湖庄园]。我不常去，这是因为如果我们作为朋友交谈，我想尽可能直率和诚实。如果我们是专业人士，我只需要能够问他任何我需要问的问题。期间。没什么。没有任何限制。

paras.en: “He’s never asked for questions ahead of an interview. I’ve never given him questions out of an interview,” he adds. “He lets me be myself, and you know, it just endures because he understands and respects what I’m doing, and I respect that he’s the President of our country now.”
paras.zh: “他从来没有在面试前问过问题。我也从来没有在面试后问过他问题，”他补充道。 “他让我做我自己，你知道，这种感觉之所以能持续下去，是因为他理解并尊重我正在做的事情，我尊重他现在是我们国家的总统。”

paras.en: But as jealous as other news executives may be of Fox’s ratings, two TV news veterans (one currently at a competitor, and one former competitor) says that it is Fox’s spending on digital that really make them jealous.
paras.zh: 但正如其他新闻高管可能对福克斯的收视率感到嫉妒一样，两名电视新闻资深人士（一名目前在竞争对手，一名前竞争对手）表示，真正让他们嫉妒的是福克斯在数字方面的支出。

paras.en: Fox News’ digital efforts, to be certain, are not a replacement for the linear business, but Fox Nation launched nearly eight years ago, and has found a niche with documentaries and entertainment fare that is seen as a complement to the channel, which also streams live through Fox One.
paras.zh: 可以肯定的是，福克斯新闻的数字化努力并不能取代线性业务，但福克斯国家频道在近八年前推出，并在纪录片和娱乐节目中找到了一个利基市场，这被视为对该频道的补充，该频道也通过福克斯一号进行直播。

paras.en: And Fox, acutely aware of the competition that conservative talk podcasts present, has poured significant resources into the digital space, acquiring and launching podcasts like Ruthless, The Riley Gaines Show and Will Cain Country, as well as shows that lean on Fox talent like The Girls and Hannity’s show Hang Out, where he does longform interviews about politics, pop culture, and even topics out of left field like UAPs and the afterlife.
paras.zh: 福克斯敏锐地意识到保守派谈话播客所带来的竞争，因此在数字领域投入了大量资源，收购并推出了《Ruthless》、《The Riley Gaines Show》和《Will Cain Country》等播客，以及依赖福克斯人才的节目，如《The Girls》和《Hannity》的节目《Hang Out》，他在其中对政治、流行文化，甚至像 UAP 和来世这样的左翼话题进行长篇采访。

paras.en: “It gives you a chance to really just lay back and go deeper into issues and into people that I find refreshing and kind of scratches a niche for me,” he says. “I’m a worker. I like to work. So if I’m not working, I’m bored.”
paras.zh: 他说：“它让你有机会真正放松下来，更深入地研究问题和人，让我觉得耳目一新，对我来说有点新奇。” “我是一名工人。我喜欢工作。所以如果我不工作，我就会感到无聊。”

paras.en: And while the conservative podcast landscape is cluttered, with shows like Candace Owens and Ben Shapiro still holding large audiences (not to mention programs from former Fox hosts like Megyn Kelly and Tucker Carlson), the company has even found a way to benefit indirectly from that, with Red Seat Ventures operating out of Fox’s Tubi division, and providing services to former Fox News talent in the podcast space.
paras.zh: 尽管保守派播客格局混乱，坎迪斯·欧文斯和本·夏皮罗等节目仍然拥有大量观众（更不用说梅根·凯利和塔克·卡尔森等前福克斯主持人的节目），但该公司甚至找到了一种间接从中受益的方法，红座风险投资公司在福克斯的 Tubi 部门运营，并为播客领域的前福克斯新闻人才提供服务。

paras.en: Still, there is a generational divide at play, and the repercussions could still be felt. As any TV veteran will tell you, the digital business is simply smaller and more cutthroat than traditional TV, and if linear continues to decline at the pace it has for the last decade, every TV news outlet will face the financial consequences, and Fox is no exception.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，代沟仍然存在，其影响仍然可以感受到。正如任何一位电视老手都会告诉你的那样，数字业务比传统电视规模更小、更残酷，如果线性电视继续以过去十年的速度下滑，每个电视新闻媒体都将面临财务后果，福克斯也不例外。

paras.en: “The traditional people want to get their morning cup of joe, and they want to hear the news of the day, your reaction, your authentic opinion about what’s happening,” Jones says. “Then there’s the people of my generation, the younger generation that just wants sound bites, they want TikTok-ification. You have to serve both of them.”
paras.zh: “传统的人们想要早上喝一杯咖啡，他们想听听当天的新闻、你的反应、你对正在发生的事情的真实看法，”琼斯说。 “还有我这一代人，年轻一代只想要原声片段，他们想要 TikTok 化。你必须为他们两者服务。”

paras.en: Even that, however, could be an opportunity. Tarlov says that, based on her research on younger consumers, they are much more open to consuming media from people they disagree with.
paras.zh: 然而，即便如此，也可能是一个机会。塔洛夫说，根据她对年轻消费者的研究，他们更愿意消费与他们意见不同的人的媒体。

paras.en: “They’re not as siloed, they created the debate vertical on TikTok, for instance. That’s because young people want to see folks talking to each other,” she says. “There is such a genuine interest to listen to people with alternative points of view and see how they represent their beliefs versus this person that believes strongly in their particular worldview. So I think that’s really heartening and exciting for the future.”
paras.zh: “他们没有那么孤立，例如，他们在 TikTok 上创建了垂直辩论。这是因为年轻人希望看到人们互相交谈，”她说。 “人们非常有兴趣倾听持不同观点的人的意见，看看他们如何代表自己的信仰，而不是那些坚信自己特定世界观的人。所以我认为这对未来来说真的令人振奋和兴奋。”

paras.en: And it’s an opportunity for TV news operations, regardless of their political leanings.
paras.zh: 这对电视新闻运营来说是一个机会，无论他们的政治倾向如何。

paras.en: But there may be one other thing that makes Fox, Fox. And that’s Hannity himself. Both Perino and Jones credit him with getting their start at the channel and helping to hone their on-air personalities.
paras.zh: 但可能还有另一件事造就了福克斯，福克斯。这就是汉尼蒂本人。佩里诺和琼斯都认为他是他们在频道的起步者，并帮助磨练了他们的广播个性。

paras.en: Hannity, for his part, isn’t one to dissuade that perception of himself as the channel’s in-house talent scout and professional booster.
paras.zh: 就汉尼蒂而言，他并没有否认自己是频道内部的星探和专业助推器。

paras.en: He recalls an event he attended with both Trump and Rupert Murdoch.
paras.zh: 他回忆起他与特朗普和鲁珀特·默多克一起参加的一次活动。

paras.en: “The President goes [to Murdoch] ‘why do you even pay him? He’ll do it for free.’ I’m looking at him and I’m like, ‘will you please shush if you mind?’” he recalls. “But there was a certain degree of truth in that statement. Although I wouldn’t do it for free.”
paras.zh: “总统（对默多克）说，‘你为什么要付钱给他？他会免费做这件事。’我看着他，心想，‘如果你介意的话，请闭嘴吧？’”他回忆道。 “但这句话有一定程度的真实性。尽管我不会免费这样做。”

articles.title: DOJ sues to block Alaska from certifying Senate race winner if Republican narrowly loses

paras.en: The Department of Justice filed an extraordinary lawsuit seeking to block Alaska from certifying the winner of its upcoming U.S. Senate election if incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses.
paras.zh: 如果现任共和党参议员丹·沙利文输了，司法部提起了一项特别诉讼，试图阻止阿拉斯加州确认即将举行的美国参议院选举的获胜者。

paras.en: The lawsuit cites what it argues is likely voter confusion from the name of another candidate, retired teacher Daniel J. Sullivan, on the ballot.
paras.zh: 该诉讼援引了选票上另一位候选人、退休教师丹尼尔·J·沙利文(Daniel J. Sullivan)的名字，认为这可能会让选民感到困惑。

paras.en: The DOJ says that could help Democratic nominee Mary Peltola defeat the incumbent, Dan S. Sullivan, in what is expected to be a close contest.
paras.zh: 美国司法部表示，这可能有助于民主党候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉 (Mary Peltola) 在一场预计势均力敌的竞争中击败现任总统丹·S·沙利文 (Dan S. Sullivan)。

paras.en: "The United States accordingly brings this lawsuit to protect the integrity of the 2026 Senate election in Alaska," says the suit filed Thursday in U.S. District Court in Alaska.
paras.zh: 周四向阿拉斯加州美国地方法院提起的诉讼称：“美国因此提起此诉讼，以保护阿拉斯加 2026 年参议院选举的完整性。”

paras.en: The suit asks a federal judge in Alaska to bar the state from certifying "any result that may be impacted by voter confusion ... pending an investigation to determine whether votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan were meant to be cast for Senator Sullivan."
paras.zh: 该诉讼要求阿拉斯加州的一名联邦法官禁止该州认证“任何可能受到选民混乱影响的结果……等待调查以确定投票给丹尼尔·J·沙利文的票是否应该投给参议员沙利文”。

paras.en: The suit alleges that Daniel J. Sullivan's "sole purpose" of running for the Senate "is to benefit the Peltola campaign by reducing the number of votes for Senator Sullivan." Sullivan only registered as Republican earlier this year, previously having been a member of the Alaska Independence Party.
paras.zh: 该诉讼称，丹尼尔·J·沙利文竞选参议员的“唯一目的”是“通过减少沙利文参议员的票数来使佩尔托拉竞选活动受益”。沙利文今年早些时候才注册为共和党人，此前曾是阿拉斯加独立党成员。

paras.en: The Alaska race is one of several Senate contests in November that could determine whether Republicans retain their slim majority in the upper chamber of Congress.
paras.zh: 阿拉斯加竞选是11月份的几场参议院竞选之一，这些竞选可能决定共和党是否能在国会上议院保住微弱多数席位。

paras.en: The Cook Political Report with Amy Walter rates the Alaska Senate race as one of seven "toss-up" contests for that chamber. The election tracking site FiftyPlusOne's average of polling shows Peltola, a former U.S. House member from Alaska, with just a two-point lead over Sullivan.
paras.zh: 艾米·沃尔特 (Amy Walter) 的库克政治报告将阿拉斯加州参议员竞选评为该院七场“难以预测”的竞选之一。选举跟踪网站 FiftyPlusOne 的平均民意调查显示，来自阿拉斯加州的前美国众议院议员佩尔托拉仅领先沙利文两点。

paras.en: The suit came hours after President Donald Trump, in a Truth Social post, wrote, "I am very concerned about the Dan S. Sullivan Race for the U.S. Senate in Alaska in that it is totally confusing, with the Dumocrats putting up another man, totally unrelated to Politics, named Daniel J. Sullivan, Jr."
paras.zh: 就在这起诉讼发生几个小时后，唐纳德·特朗普总统在《真相社会》的帖子中写道：“我对丹·S·沙利文竞选阿拉斯加州美国参议员一事感到非常担忧，因为这完全令人困惑，杜民主党派了另一个与政治完全无关的人，名叫小丹尼尔·J·沙利文。”

paras.en: "It's ridiculous that the Court didn't stop this SCAM. Even 1, 2, or 3% could make the difference," Trump said.
paras.zh: “可笑的是，法院没有阻止这种骗局。即使是 1%、2% 或 3% 也能产生影响，”特朗普说。

paras.en: "We are looking at powerful legal options to remove the fraudulent Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. from the Ballot, and holding the Democrats accountable for their Election Interference, in the pursuit of Justice and Fairness."
paras.zh: “我们正在寻找强有力的法律选择，将欺诈性的小丹尼尔·沙利文从选票中剔除，并追究民主党对选举干扰的责任，以追求正义和公平。”

paras.en: Alaska's general election for the Senate uses ranked-choice voting. Voters rank their candidates in order of preference. If no candidate gets more than 50% in round one, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated in the second round, and that process continues until there are just two candidates and the winner is the one with the most votes.
paras.zh: 阿拉斯加参议院大选采用排名选择投票方式。选民按照偏好顺序对候选人进行排名。如果第一轮没有候选人获得超过 50% 的支持，则得票最少的候选人将在第二轮中被淘汰，这一过程将持续下去，直到只剩下两名候选人，得票最多的候选人获胜。

paras.en: "Daniel J. Sullivan's presence on the ballot threatens to mislead Alaskan citizens who want to vote for Senator Sullivan," the suit says. "For example, some supporters of Senator Sullivan likely will inadvertently vote for Daniel J. Sullivan."
paras.zh: 诉讼称：“丹尼尔·J·沙利文出现在选票上可能会误导想要投票给沙利文参议员的阿拉斯加公民。” “例如，沙利文参议员的一些支持者可能会无意中投票给丹尼尔·沙利文。”

paras.en: "Other supporters of Senator Sullivan likely will be confused as to how to rank the three Republican candidates as to defeat Peltola," the suit says. "They might not rank Senator Sullivan at all, resulting in votes for Daniel J. Sullivan to be transferred to Peltola after Daniel J. Sullivan's all-but-guaranteed elimination in the first or second round of tabulations."
paras.zh: 诉讼称：“参议员沙利文的其他支持者可能会对如何对三名共和党候选人进行排名以击败佩尔托拉感到困惑。” “他们可能根本不会对参议员沙利文进行排名，导致丹尼尔·J·沙利文在第一轮或第二轮统计中几乎肯定被淘汰后，将投票给丹尼尔·J·沙利文的选票转移到佩尔托拉。”

paras.en: In a statement to CNBC, a DOJ spokesperson said, "Alaska's Division of Elections determined that Mr. Daniel J. Sullivan's candidacy was intended to mislead voters and compromise the fairness of the ballot."
paras.zh: 美国司法部发言人在给 CNBC 的一份声明中表示，“阿拉斯加州选举部门认定，丹尼尔·J·沙利文先生的候选资格旨在误导选民并损害投票的公平性。”

paras.en: "Therefore, the Justice Department, consistent with the National Voter Registration Act enacted by Congress, is taking the necessary steps to ensure that this frivolous candidacy does not undermine the integrity of Alaska's election or the will of its voters," the spokesperson said.
paras.zh: 发言人表示：“因此，司法部正在根据国会颁布的《国家选民登记法》采取必要措施，确保这种轻率的候选行为不会损害阿拉斯加选举的完整性或选民的意愿。”

paras.en: Nate Adams, the campaign spokesman for Sen. Sullivan, said, "We'll let the DOJ complaint run its course."
paras.zh: 参议员沙利文的竞选发言人内特·亚当斯 (Nate Adams) 表示：“我们会让司法部的投诉顺其自然。”

paras.en: "Alaskans can tell the difference between a Democrat sideshow and Senator Sullivan's strong record of delivering for Alaska, a record he'll keep building on for the next six years," Adams said.
paras.zh: 亚当斯说：“阿拉斯加人可以分辨出民主党的余兴节目和沙利文参议员为阿拉斯加做出的杰出贡献之间的区别，他将在未来六年内继续保持这一记录。”

paras.en: CNBC has requested comment from Alaska's attorney general, Daniel J. Sullivan and Peltola.
paras.zh: CNBC 已要求阿拉斯加总检察长丹尼尔·J·沙利文和佩尔托拉发表评论。

paras.en: Devan Barber, director of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, in a statement to CNBC said, "Donald Trump knows that Dan Sullivan is going to lose the election, so now his Department of Justice is filing a sham lawsuit to overturn the will of Alaska voters and steal an election when he loses."
paras.zh: 民主党参议员竞选委员会主任德万·巴伯在给 CNBC 的一份声明中表示，“唐纳德·特朗普知道丹·沙利文将输掉选举，所以现在他的司法部正在提起虚假诉讼，以推翻阿拉斯加州选民的意愿，并在他输掉选举时窃取选举结果。”

paras.en: Daniel J. Sullivan received just 2.5% of the vote in Alaska's open primary on Aug. 28, but that was enough to win him one of four spots on the Senate general election ballot.
paras.zh: 丹尼尔·J·沙利文 (Daniel J. Sullivan) 在 8 月 28 日的阿拉斯加公开初选中仅获得 2.5% 的选票，但这足以为他赢得参议院大选投票的四个席位之一。

paras.en: Peltola got 49.5% in the primary, and Sen. Sullivan received 41.1%. Another Republican, Gerald Heikes, received just 1.1% of the primary vote, earning him the fourth spot on the ballot.
paras.zh: 佩尔托拉在初选中获得了 49.5% 的支持率，参议员沙利文获得了 41.1% 的支持率。另一位共和党人杰拉尔德·海克斯 (Gerald Heikes) 仅获得 1.1% 的初选选票，排名第四。

paras.en: Although Daniel J. Sullivan sought to run as a Republican, the Division of Elections decided not to list that party next to his name on the general election ballot. His name is spelled out, "Daniel J. Sullivan," and there are no other words on that line.
paras.zh: 尽管丹尼尔·J·沙利文寻求以共和党身份参选，但选举部决定不在大选选票上将该政党列在他的名字旁边。他的名字被拼写为“丹尼尔·J·沙利文”，并且该行上没有其他单词。

paras.en: Both Sen. Sullivan, who has been in the Senate since 2015, and Heikes have the words "registered Republican" in parentheses next to their names.
paras.zh: 自 2015 年以来一直在参议院任职的参议员沙利文和海克斯的名字旁边的括号里都有“注册共和党人”字样。

paras.en: And Sen. Sullivan, listed on the ballot as Dan. S. Sullivan, also has the word "incumbent" next to his name.
paras.zh: 还有参议员沙利文，选票上的名字是丹。 S. Sullivan，他的名字旁边也有“现任”一词。

paras.en: — CNBC's Justin Papp contributed to this article.
paras.zh: — CNBC 的贾斯汀·帕普 (Justin Papp) 对本文做出了贡献。

articles.title: Texas Senate race: New Talarico ad rips Elon Musk 'dark money' push

paras.en: James Talarico's campaign hit back at Elon Musk Thursday, calling the 2026 election cycle's top spender out for his cash infusion in the Texas Senate race amid an ongoing feud between the Democratic nominee and the world's richest man.
paras.zh: 周四，詹姆斯·塔拉里科(James Talarico)的竞选团队对埃隆·马斯克(Elon Musk)进行了回击，称2026年选举周期中支出最高的人因在民主党候选人与世界首富之间持续不和的情况下在德克萨斯州参议院竞选中注入现金而出局。

paras.en: A video posted by the Talarico campaign's account on X Thursday of a new ad targets Musk for his record spending in favor of Republican nominee Ken Paxton, telling him "Texas is not for sale."
paras.zh: 塔拉里科竞选团队周四发布的一段新广告视频针对马斯克为共和党候选人肯·帕克斯顿（Ken Paxton）创纪录的支出，告诉他“德克萨斯州是非卖品”。

paras.en: "Do you keep seeing these attack ads against James Talarico? Look a little closer. The same super PACs are paying for nearly all of them," the video's narrator intones. "But who's funding these dark money groups? Elon Musk."
paras.zh: “你经常看到这些针对詹姆斯·塔拉里科的攻击广告吗？再仔细看看。几乎所有这些广告都是由同一个超级政治行动委员会支付的，”视频旁白说道。 “但是谁在资助这些黑钱集团呢？埃隆·马斯克。”

paras.en: "He's almost single-handedly bankrolling the effort to install Ken Paxton in the U.S. Senate," the narrator continues.
paras.zh: “他几乎单枪匹马地资助肯·帕克斯顿进入美国参议院，”旁白继续说道。

paras.en: "Elon wants to buy up our land, he wants to buy up our water, and now, he wants to buy his own personal U.S. senator. He knows that if his millions drag the most corrupt politician in Texas across the finish line, Ken Paxton will owe him everything."
paras.zh: “埃隆想买下我们的土地，他想买下我们的水，现在，他想买下他自己的美国参议员。他知道，如果他的数百万美元拖着德克萨斯州最腐败的政客冲过终点线，肯·帕克斯顿将欠他一切。”

paras.en: The new ad dropped with less than two weeks until the midterm election and amid an ongoing feud between Talarico and Musk.
paras.zh: 距离中期选举还有不到两周的时间，在塔拉里科和马斯克之间持续不和的情况下，这则新广告就被停播了。

paras.en: In a post Wednesday on X, Musk said, "There is something deeply wrong with James Talarico." And on Thursday, he wrote on X that "Talarico hates Texas and America" while reposting a video about voter-ID requirements.
paras.zh: 周三，马斯克在 X 上发帖称，“詹姆斯·塔拉里科存在严重问题。”周四，他在 X 上写道，“塔拉里科讨厌德克萨斯州和美国”，同时转发了一段有关选民身份要求的视频。

paras.en: Talarico fired back Wednesday, replying to the earlier post, "There is something deeply wrong with a political system that allows one trillionaire to buy his own personal U.S. Senator."
paras.zh: 塔拉里科周三进行了反击，回复了之前的帖子，“允许一位万亿富翁购买自己的美国参议员的政治制度存在严重错误。”

paras.en: The Tesla and SpaceX CEO has spent around $366 million across 40 races so far in the midterms, based on CNBC's calculations, making Musk the largest individual donor of the cycle. Much of that spending is based in Texas, where he moved his corporate headquarters and personal primary residence.
paras.zh: 根据 CNBC 的计算，特斯拉和 SpaceX 的首席执行官迄今为止在中期选举的 40 场比赛中花费了约 3.66 亿美元，使马斯克成为该周期最大的个人捐助者。大部分支出都在德克萨斯州，他将公司总部和个人主要住所搬到了那里。

paras.en: At least $189.6 million of Musk's political spend has been, through various methods, in support of Paxton, the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Texas and Talarico's opponent. An average of polls aggregated by FiftyPlusOne show Talarico with a 3-percentage-point advantage over Paxton as of Oct. 23.
paras.zh: 马斯克的政治支出中至少有 1.896 亿美元通过各种方式支持了德克萨斯州美国参议院共和党候选人、塔拉里科的对手帕克斯顿。截至 10 月 23 日，FiftyPlusOne 汇总的民意调查平均显示，Talarico 比 Paxton 领先 3 个百分点。

articles.title: 10-year Treasury yield drops back to 5% this week as investors seek cover from AI worries

paras.en: Investors ran for cover this week as artificial intelligence fears and higher oil prices hit stocks, driving the yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note below 5%.
paras.zh: 由于对人工智能的担忧和油价上涨冲击股市，投资者本周纷纷寻求避险，导致 10 年期美国国债收益率跌破 5%。

paras.en: The benchmark yield was just under 5% on Friday, after falling beneath that level Thursday for the first time in a month, as investors continued to express misgivings over the massive debt tech companies are taking on to finance their build-out of AI networks.
paras.zh: 周五基准收益率略低于 5%，继周四一个月来首次跌破该水平后，投资者继续对科技公司为建设人工智能网络融资而承担的巨额债务表示担忧。

paras.en: Investors are also weighing higher energy prices as the Iran war drags on and are looking ahead to next week's Federal Reserve meeting, said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth.
paras.zh: B. Riley Wealth 首席市场策略师阿特·霍根 (Art Hogan) 表示，随着伊朗战争的持续，投资者也在权衡能源价格上涨，并期待下周的美联储会议。

paras.en: "The massive selling of Treasurys in the month of September, bringing yields up by close to 50 basis points, clearly got ahead of itself," he said. "What we're seeing over the last two weeks is the slow unwind of that trade back to what is likely a more normalized level of yield."
paras.zh: 他表示：“9月份美国国债的大规模抛售使收益率上升了近50个基点，这显然是有些过头了。” “过去两周我们看到的是，交易缓慢回落至可能更为正常化的收益率水平。”

paras.en: On Friday, the yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury — used as a benchmark for borrowing costs including mortgages — rose more than 3 basis points to 4.99%.
paras.zh: 周五，作为包括抵押贷款在内的借贷成本基准的 10 年期美国国债收益率上涨超过 3 个基点，至 4.99%。

paras.en: The yield on the 2-year Treasury note, which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve policy, increased by 5 basis points to 4.686%. Yields on longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasurys climbed nearly 3 basis points to 5.315%.
paras.zh: 更贴近美联储短期政策的2年期国债收益率上升5个基点至4.686%。 30年期较长期美国国债收益率攀升近3个基点至5.315%。

paras.en: One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.
paras.zh: 一个基点等于 0.01%，即 1% 的 1/100，收益率和价格走势成反比。

paras.en: This week's rebound in Treasury prices comes just weeks after 10- and 30-year yields jumped to their highest levels in more than 20 years.
paras.zh: 本周，美国国债价格出现反弹，而就在几周前，10 年期和 30 年期国债收益率跃升至 20 多年来的最高水平。

paras.en: Since then, concerns have grown about the hundreds of billions of dollars being spent by tech companies. Stocks sank, bond yields on outstanding tech debt rose and spreads on credit default swaps widened in a host of AI companies.
paras.zh: 从那时起，人们对科技公司花费的数千亿美元的担忧与日俱增。许多人工智能公司的股市下跌，未偿科技债务的债券收益率上升，信用违约掉期利差扩大。

paras.en: CoreWeave has led the rout. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 stands at 15.75%, while the spread on its five-year credit default swaps is 1,140. Any reading above 1,000 is generally considered distressed.
paras.zh: CoreWeave 引领了这场溃败。 2031年到期的9.75%债券收益率为15.75%，五年期信用违约掉期利差为1,140。任何超过 1,000 的读数通常都被认为是痛苦的。

paras.en: The question remains whether the trend of lower Treasury yields will continue, said Byron Anderson, head of fixed income at Laffer Tengler Investments.
paras.zh: Laffer Tengler Investments 固定收益主管拜伦·安德森 (Byron Anderson) 表示，问题仍然是国债收益率下降的趋势是否会持续。

paras.en: "With a Federal Reserve that is focused on inflation and largely out of the bond market as a buyer, it is hard to see a sustained rally without the market narrative flipping to recession," he said. "We are far from the recession narrative, with two Fed rate hikes still built into expectations and a good economic backdrop."
paras.zh: 他表示：“由于美联储专注于通胀，并且作为买家基本上退出债券市场，因此很难看到股市持续上涨而不导致市场叙事转向衰退。” “我们距离衰退的叙述还很远，美联储两次加息仍然建立在预期和良好的经济背景之下。”

paras.en: The Federal Reserve meets next week and the market isn't expecting any change in official rates from the current level of 3.75% to 4.00%. However, it is pricing in a roughly 78% probability of a quarter percentage point hike in December, according to the CME Group FedWatch tool.
paras.zh: 美联储下周将召开会议，市场预计官方利率不会从目前的 3.75% 调整至 4.00%。然而，根据 CME 集团 FedWatch 工具的数据，12 月份加息 25 个百分点的可能性约为 78%。

paras.en: "At this stage, the tightening of financial conditions hasn't been dramatic enough to preclude another rate hike this year, although a sustained deterioration could readily alter the Fed's policy calculus," BMO Capital Markets' credit strategy team said in a note Friday.
paras.zh: BMO资本市场信贷策略团队周五在一份报告中表示，“现阶段，金融状况收紧的幅度还不足以排除今年再次加息的可能性，尽管持续恶化可能很容易改变美联储的政策考量。”

paras.en: Consumer sentiment changed little in October from historically low levels as inflation weighed on the economic outlook, according to a University of Michigan survey released Friday.
paras.zh: 密歇根大学周五发布的一项调查显示，由于通胀对经济前景构成压力，十月份消费者信心与历史低位相比变化不大。

paras.en: The survey showed the headline consumer sentiment index at 48 for the end of the month, off just 0.1 point from September and better than the Dow Jones consensus for 46.3. Compared with a year ago, the gauge tumbled 10.4%.
paras.zh: 调查显示，本月底总体消费者信心指数为 48，仅比 9 月份低 0.1 点，好于道琼斯平均指数 46.3。与一年前相比，该指数下跌了 10.4%。

paras.en: On inflation, the one-year outlook rose to 4.7%, while the five-year expectation accelerated to 3.5%, both 0.1 percentage point higher than September.
paras.zh: 通胀方面，一年期预期升至4.7%，五年期预期升至3.5%，均较9月份上升0.1个百分点。

paras.en: Also on Friday, the S&P Global Purchasing Managers Index for manufacturing came in hotter than expected, at 56 versus a 55.3 estimate, the highest reading in 53 months.
paras.zh: 同样在周五，标准普尔全球制造业采购经理指数为 56，高于预期的 55.3，为 53 个月来的最高值。

paras.en: Meanwhile, rising energy costs continue to weigh on the inflation outlook.
paras.zh: 与此同时，能源成本上涨继续给通胀前景带来压力。

paras.en: West Texas Intermediate futures for December delivery climbed more than 3% to top $102 a barrel on Friday, while Brent crude, the international oil benchmark, traded almost 3% higher at roughly $116 a barrel.
paras.zh: 周五，12 月交割的西德克萨斯中质原油期货上涨超过 3%，达到每桶 102 美元，而国际石油基准布伦特原油则上涨近 3%，至每桶约 116 美元。

paras.en: Firmer energy prices come as fresh attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabian oil installations drove new fears over an oil supply squeeze. Reports earlier this week suggested that the U.S. and Israel could resume strikes against Iran following the midterm elections on Nov. 3.
paras.zh: 伊朗支持的胡塞武装分子对沙特阿拉伯石油设施的新袭击引发了人们对石油供应紧张的新担忧，能源价格走强。本周早些时候的报道暗示，美国和以色列可能会在 11 月 3 日中期选举后恢复对伊朗的打击。

paras.en: — CNBC's Jeff Cox contributed reporting.
paras.zh: — CNBC 的杰夫·考克斯 (Jeff Cox) 贡献了报道。

articles.title: How the brain handles uncertainty, and why resilience matters

paras.en: Rachel Feltman: For Scientific American’s Science Quickly, I’m Rachel Feltman.
paras.zh: 雷切尔·费尔特曼：《科学美国人》的《科学快报》，我是雷切尔·费尔特曼。

paras.en: There’s a lot of uncertainty in the air right now, whether you’re trying to predict the outcome of an upcoming election or just trying to guess how much it will cost to gas up your car come next week. You don’t need a degree in neuroscience to know that all those unknowns are tough for the human brain to handle. But some experts think there’s actually a lot of nuance to explore about the cognitive burden of uncertainty—and that you might actually have the power to change how well you tackle it.
paras.zh: 现在空气中存在很多不确定性，无论您是想预测即将到来的选举结果，还是只是想猜测下周给您的汽车加油需要多少钱。你不需要神经科学学位就知道所有这些未知因素对于人脑来说都是难以处理的。但一些专家认为，关于不确定性的认知负担，实际上有很多细微差别需要探索——而且你实际上可能有能力改变你处理它的方式。

paras.en: Our guest today is Maia Szalavitz, a contributing opinion writer for the New York Times and the author or co-author of eight books. She’s also the author of a feature in the latest issue of Scientific American that explores the emerging science of the human brain as a prediction engine. She’s here to tell us more about what that means in a world that feels increasingly unpredictable—and what we can do to make our minds more adaptable to chaos.
paras.zh: 今天我们的嘉宾是 Maia Szalavitz，她是《纽约时报》的撰稿人，也是八本书的作者或合著者。她还是最新一期《科学美国人》中一篇专题的作者，该专题探讨了人脑作为预测引擎的新兴科学。她来这里是为了告诉我们，在一个越来越难以预测的世界中，这意味着什么，以及我们可以做些什么来让我们的思想更适应混乱。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Thank you so much for coming on to chat with us.
paras.zh: 非常感谢您接受我们的采访。

paras.en: Feltman: So how did you first get interested in this topic?.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：那么您最初是如何对这个话题感兴趣的呢？

paras.en: Szalavitz: Sure. So our world seems to be becoming increasingly uncertain, and it’s not the kind of uncertainty that we’re used to dealing with in modern America because we’re used to the law being predictable. We’re used to the government’s actions being reasonably predictable. We’re used to all kinds of norms that are being violated. We’re used to being able to think of “What do I wanna be when I grow up?” and that be an actual thing that you can choose rather than perhaps losing all jobs to AI.
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：当然。因此，我们的世界似乎变得越来越不确定，这不是我们在现代美国习惯处理的那种不确定性，因为我们习惯了法律的可预测性。我们已经习惯了政府的行为是可以合理预测的。我们已经习惯了各种被违反的规范。我们习惯于思考“长大后我想做什么？”这是你可以选择的实际事情，而不是让所有工作岗位都被人工智能夺走。

paras.en: So I was in the midst of my own uncertainty, and I’ve been thinking a lot about this idea of how the brain works as a prediction engine, and I was really interested in hearing from people with that perspective about, like, how to manage in this really unusual situation—I mean, I didn’t even get to mention climate change. You’re used to, like, summer being summer and winter being winter—so it’s really unsettling and really, you know, because our brains do work, as far as we can tell, as prediction engines, and we’re constantly having to update prediction errors, when there’s uncertainty, it gives your brain a lot more work.
paras.zh: 所以我自己也处于不确定之中，我一直在思考大脑如何作为预测引擎工作的想法，我真的很想听听持这种观点的人的意见，比如如何在这种非常不寻常的情况下进行管理——我的意思是，我什至没有提到气候变化。你已经习惯了，夏天就是夏天，冬天就是冬天——所以这真的很令人不安，你知道，因为据我们所知，我们的大脑确实作为预测引擎在工作，而且我们不断地必须更新预测错误，当存在不确定性时，它会给你的大脑带来更多的工作。

paras.en: Feltman: What exactly do we mean when we say we’re modeling the brain as a prediction engine?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：当我们说我们正在将大脑建模为预测引擎时，我们到底是什么意思？

paras.en: Szalavitz: So essentially, all of our experience of reality is a hallucination under this perspective, which is really weird to think about just in itself. But essentially, in order to solve the problem of avoiding entropy and avoiding death and ideally successfully reproducing, biological creatures need a way of managing risk and figuring out what to do next.
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：从本质上讲，从这个角度来看，我们对现实的所有体验都是幻觉，这本身就很奇怪。但本质上，为了解决避免熵和避免死亡以及理想情况下成功繁殖的问题，生物需要一种管理风险并弄清楚下一步该做什么的方法。

paras.en: And so our brains sort of optimize on, okay, we get this general sense—and it’s based on experience, and there’s obviously some genetics—but you start out with this general, you know, way of perceiving the world, and then you update it when there’s an error. And so, you know, my example that I use in the piece is that, like, if you are in your room, and you have a cat, and you look, and you see something out of your corner of your eye, and it’s curled up, and it’s gray, you have a pretty full picture of that cat in your head when you, you know, do that. And then you look, and, oh, it’s actually the towel that you forgot to put in the laundry, right? But there’s no, like, glitch in it going from cat to towel, right? It’s, like, completely seamless, and this is the way our entire world works. And there’s all kinds of really interesting implications of it for things like pain and how you act psychologically.
paras.zh: 所以我们的大脑在某种程度上进行了优化，好吧，我们得到了这种一般感觉——它是基于经验的，而且显然有一些遗传因素——但你从这种普遍的、你知道的、感知世界的方式开始，然后当出现错误时你会更新它。所以，你知道，我在这篇文章中使用的例子是，如果你在你的房间里，你有一只猫，你看，你从你的眼角看到一些东西，它卷曲着，它是灰色的，当你这样做时，你的脑海里就有了那只猫的完整画面。然后你一看，哦，这实际上是你忘记放进洗衣机的毛巾，对吗？但从猫到毛巾的过程中不会出现任何问题，对吧？它就像是完全无缝的，这就是我们整个世界的运作方式。它对疼痛和心理行为等方面有各种非常有趣的影响。

paras.en: But that is kind of the fundamental idea, that we are always making predictions, revising predictions, and, you know, with major prediction errors, it becomes seriously problematic because we may not be able to, you know, eat and survive and do the things we need to do.
paras.zh: 但这是基本的想法，我们总是在做出预测，修改预测，而且，你知道，如果出现重大预测错误，它就会成为严重的问题，因为你知道，我们可能无法吃饭、生存和做我们需要做的事情。

paras.en: Feltman: So what are some of the implications for, you know, what this means in terms of, like, how we think things through and how we process the world? I guess what I’m getting at is, like, “Why is it helpful to use this prediction engine idea?”
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：那么，你知道，这对我们如何思考事物以及我们如何处理世界意味着什么？我想我的意思是，“为什么使用这个预测引擎的想法有帮助？”

paras.en: Szalavitz: If you think about it, if your entire life is based on predictions, there are certain things that you are going to be good at and certain things you are going to be bad at. Staying in the moment is going to be a very difficult thing if your entire world is predictions, right? And if you’re constantly predicting things, then what you’re predicting has a very big influence on what you will perceive.
paras.zh: Szalavitz：如果你想一想，如果你的整个生活都基于预测，那么有些事情你会擅长，有些事情你会不擅长。如果你的整个世界都是预测，那么停留在当下将是一件非常困难的事情，对吧？如果你不断地预测事情，那么你的预测会对你的感知产生很大的影响。

paras.en: And so if you are constantly seeing the world in a really negative way, that will skew it even further. Or if you are constantly just trying to avoid things, it’s really, if you think about it, it has implications for absolutely every aspect, which is why I’m sort of struggling of, like, narrowing it down here.
paras.zh: 因此，如果你不断地以一种非常消极的方式看待世界，那就会使世界更加扭曲。或者，如果你不断地试图避免一些事情，事实上，如果你仔细想想，它对每个方面都有影响，这就是为什么我有点挣扎，比如，缩小范围。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah, absolutely. What about the implications for how cognitive stress impacts our bodies?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的，绝对如此。认知压力对我们的身体有何影响？

paras.en: Szalavitz: Sure. So Bruce McEwen was the great researcher on the impact of stress and health, right? And he talks about, like, how stress gets under the skin. And at this very moment, I am having a personal experience of this because I had to take a course of prednisone to deal with a hearing issue, and that’s basically massive amounts of stress hormones, like, coursing through me and making me feel like bad coke or something.
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：当然。所以布鲁斯·麦克尤恩是研究压力和健康影响的伟大研究者，对吧？他谈到了压力是如何渗透到皮肤下面的。就在此时此刻，我对此有亲身经历，因为我必须服用泼尼松疗程来解决听力问题，这基本上是大量的压力荷尔蒙，就像在我体内流动，让我感觉像喝了难喝的可乐之类的东西。

paras.en: But those stress hormones are really good in an emergency because what they do is keep you awake and alert and focused on dealing with what you need to deal with in front of you to escape the emergency. And that has a physiological cost because you spend more energy doing it, and therefore you produce more waste, and therefore there’s all kinds of different things that your body needs to manage that can get out of whack.
paras.zh: 但这些压力荷尔蒙在紧急情况下确实很有用，因为它们的作用是让你保持清醒和警觉，并专注于处理你需要处理的事情，以逃避紧急情况。这会产生生理成本，因为你会花费更多的能量来做这件事，因此会产生更多的废物，因此你的身体需要管理各种不同的东西，这些东西可能会出现问题。

paras.en: And when you look at the data, severe chronic stress, starting in childhood with things like abuse or neglect or other forms of trauma, raise risk for everything from, you know, obesity, heart disease, stroke, all of the mental illnesses, virtually. And it’s because of the way these hormones impact your brain, because if you have too much of these glucocorticoids, it can eat your hippocampus a little bit, and so it makes memory weird.
paras.zh: 当你查看数据时，你会发现，严重的慢性压力，从童年时期开始，伴随着虐待、忽视或其他形式的创伤，实际上会增加肥胖、心脏病、中风和所有精神疾病等各种疾病的风险。这是因为这些激素影响你的大脑的方式，因为如果你体内的糖皮质激素过多，它会稍微吃掉你的海马体，所以它会让记忆变得奇怪。

paras.en: And a lot of these things are all about trade-offs, because in the short term, if you don’t survive, then the rest doesn’t matter, right? But in the long term, you are generating a debt in some sense.
paras.zh: 而很多这些事情都是关于权衡的，因为在短期内，如果你不能生存，那么剩下的就不重要了，对吧？但从长远来看，你在某种意义上正在产生债务。

paras.en: Feltman: Well, speaking of mental illness, in your piece, you outlined how a few mental illnesses could be reframed as sort of disruptions in this predictive machinery. Could you tell us a little bit more about that?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：嗯，说到精神疾病，在您的文章中，您概述了如何将一些精神疾病重新定义为这种预测机制的某种破坏。您能告诉我们更多相关信息吗？

paras.en: Szalavitz: Sure. So the most obvious one is anxiety, because anxiety is worrying about the future.
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：当然。所以最明显的就是焦虑，因为焦虑就是对未来的担忧。

paras.en: Szalavitz: And so uncertainty is not going to be good for anxiety. And one of the things that was really interesting about this is that if we’re in this predictive world, then one of the key ways of dealing with anxiety is to get your predictions in line with reality as much as possible. But you can get stuck if you try to do that by just escaping because if you go in a dark room and curl up, yeah, you’re gonna reduce prediction error ’cause nothing’s going on, but you are not going to get the information you need to be able to manage the world. And so people with anxiety disorders tend to have a very high intolerance of uncertainty. We just don’t like it.
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：因此，不确定性不会有利于焦虑。真正有趣的事情之一是，如果我们处于这个预测世界，那么处理焦虑的关键方法之一就是让你的预测尽可能与现实相符。但如果你试图通过逃跑来做到这一点，你可能会陷入困境，因为如果你走进一个黑暗的房间并蜷缩起来，是的，你会减少预测错误，因为什么都没有发生，但你不会获得管理世界所需的信息。因此，患有焦虑症的人往往对不确定性有很高的容忍度。我们只是不喜欢它。

paras.en: I am on the autism spectrum, and I like things to be predictable. I am not into extreme variability most of the time, except for in intellectual pursuits. But if you’re constantly having to worry about what’s gonna happen—am I gonna go out the door and get hit by a car? Or, does that person hate me?—then you’re spending a lot of mental energy, and if you start avoiding, then you will think that, like, you know, “Oh, I’m scared of dogs. I will avoid dogs. Didn’t get bitten. It worked. My strategy’s good. I will continue avoiding.” And so that creates a negative cycle that you can really get stuck in. And so while everyone with anxiety does not want to stop avoiding the things that they are avoiding, that is inevitably part of overcoming it.
paras.zh: 我属于自闭症谱系，我喜欢事情是可预测的。大多数时候，除了智力追求之外，我并不喜欢极端的变化。但如果你总是担心会发生什么——我会出门被车撞吗？或者，那个人讨厌我吗？——那么你就花费了很多精神能量，如果你开始回避，那么你会想，就像，你知道，“哦，我害怕狗。我会避开狗。没有被咬。它有效。我的策略很好。我会继续回避。”因此，这会造成一个你真的会陷入的负面循环。因此，虽然每个患有焦虑症的人都不想停止避免他们正在避免的事情，但这不可避免地是克服它的一部分。

paras.en: Feltman: The researchers that you spoke to, published something about four phenotypes for managing uncertainty. Could you tell us what those are?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：与您交谈的研究人员发表了有关管理不确定性的四种表型的文章。你能告诉我们那些是什么吗？

paras.en: Szalavitz: The first one is probably where I would constitutionally fall, which is fragile. And what that means is: does not like uncertainty, tries to hide in a dark room, is congenitally oversensitive to stimulation. Or there’s another way to get into the fragile pathway, which is by, like, abuse or neglect or growing up in a really unpredictable situation. And so you kind of turn toward dysfunctional strategies like just hiding rather than actually exploring the world and resolving the prediction errors in a productive way.
paras.zh: Szalavitz：第一个可能是我的体质会下降的地方，这是脆弱的。这意味着：不喜欢不确定性，试图躲在黑暗的房间里，对刺激先天过度敏感。或者还有另一种方法可以进入脆弱的道路，比如虐待或忽视，或者在一个真正不可预测的情况下成长。因此，你会转向功能失调的策略，比如只是隐藏而不是真正探索世界并以富有成效的方式解决预测错误。

paras.en: And so the second type is called durable, and these are people who are growing up in a very, very predictable world, which would seem to be good, but if it’s so predictable that you never experience prediction errors, and you rarely experience the stress of having to deal with unexpected things, then you’re obviously, by nature, not going to be good at it, and you may underlyingly be fragile.
paras.zh: 因此，第二种类型被称为持久型，这些人是在一个非常非常可预测的世界中长大的，这似乎很好，但如果它是如此可预测，以至于你永远不会遇到预测错误，并且你很少经历必须处理意外事情的压力，那么你显然本质上不会擅长于此，而且你可能本质上很脆弱。

paras.en: The third type is resilient, and this is what people tend to think is, “oh, this is, like, the best possible type,” because you don’t hide, you manage stress, you go and are curious about the world and learn, and by learning you build up your muscle of dealing with stress, right? But the authors of the paper argue that there’s a fourth type, which they very annoyingly call proentropic—which I would think it would be antientropic because you don’t want to die in entropy—but anyway, the point is that such people actively seek challenge and actively seek to, you know, deal with uncertainties and manage them successfully. And when you do that, you know, like anything else, the more you do something, the better you get at it generally.
paras.zh: 第三种类型是有弹性的，人们往往会认为，“哦，这就是最好的类型”，因为你不会隐藏，你会管理压力，你会对世界感到好奇并学习，通过学习你可以增强应对压力的能力，对吗？但该论文的作者认为还有第四种类型，他们非常烦人地将其称为“顺熵”（proentropic）——我认为这将是“反熵”（antientropic），因为你不想死于熵中——但无论如何，关键是这些人积极寻求挑战，积极寻求，你知道，处理不确定性并成功管理它们。当你这样做时，你知道，就像其他事情一样，你做某事越多，你通常会做得越好。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. Could you give some examples of, you know, what that would look like in the real world?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。您能否举一些例子来说明现实世界中的情况？

paras.en: Szalavitz: You could think of it as anything from, you know, a firefighter who’s going into these very intense, dangerous situations and managing extreme stress very regularly. Or you could say, well, a scientist, you know, somebody who is, daily, challenging the way they see the world and, like, putting ideas to various tests and that sort of thing. So it could just look like anybody who really is trying to not avoid the world too much. Now the thing is: sometimes avoidance is productive, and you asked earlier about other mental illnesses that can be affected by this predictive thing, and depression is really one of them. You can kind of think of depression as being “let’s curl up in a dark room,” like a strategy of that. And, you know, people argue that, evolutionarily, that may be why we have this thing that we call depression in the sense that if you’re failing, sometimes withdrawing and, like, getting out of the situation is a good idea. And if you have a mechanism to make that happen, if you’re, like, failing, like, socially or in whatever ways, then that could be productive. However, if you get stuck there, then it becomes unproductive, and obviously the feelings of it can just escalate such that it’s very difficult to escape from without, you know, chemical or therapeutic help.
paras.zh: Szalavitz：你可以把它想象成一名消防员，他经常进入这些非常紧张、危险的情况，并经常应对极端压力。或者你可以说，嗯，一个科学家，你知道，一个每天都在挑战他们看待世界的方式的人，就像将想法进行各种测试之类的。所以它看起来可能就像一个真正试图避免过多回避这个世界的人。现在的问题是：有时回避是有成效的，您之前询问过可能受这种预测性影响的其他精神疾病，而抑郁症确实是其中之一。你可以把抑郁症想象成“让我们蜷缩在一个黑暗的房间里”，就像这样的一种策略。而且，你知道，人们认为，从进化的角度来看，这可能就是为什么我们会患上抑郁症，因为如果你失败了，有时退缩，比如摆脱困境是个好主意。如果你有一个机制来实现这一点，如果你在社交方面或以任何方式失败，那么这可能是富有成效的。然而，如果你被困在那里，那么它就会变得毫无成效，而且显然它的感觉只会升级，以至于在没有化学或治疗帮助的情况下很难逃脱。

paras.en: Feltman: So can understanding the brain as a prediction engine actually help us cope better with uncertainty? Your piece certainly had a very compelling narrative lead that got into this a little bit. So maybe you could start by sharing that with our listeners.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：那么将大脑理解为预测引擎实际上可以帮助我们更好地应对不确定性吗？你的作品肯定有一个非常引人注目的叙事线索，其中涉及到这一点。所以也许你可以先与我们的听众分享这一点。

paras.en: Szalavitz: When I was interviewing the authors of the paper that described those various phenotypes, they had just survived the Eaton Fire in Los Angeles, and they had been working on the paper during that, and the fire actually threatened their homes very significantly, and they had to, like, evacuate in a smoky, messy, scary hell.
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：当我采访描述这些不同表型的论文的作者时，他们刚刚在洛杉矶伊顿火灾中幸存下来，在那段时间他们一直在写论文，而火灾实际上对他们的家园造成了非常严重的威胁，他们不得不在烟雾缭绕、混乱不堪、可怕的地狱中撤离。

paras.en: And to top it all off, one of the co-authors was injured in a childhood diving accident, and so he is quadriplegic, and he uses a wheelchair, and the mobility van that transports his wheelchair was undergoing service. So he couldn’t get into his wife’s car, and they had to leave, and he had to, like, drive his electric wheelchair through, you know, the falling debris and the howling winds and the smoke and all of that to get to a place where a vehicle could get to that would be capable of him getting picked up.
paras.zh: 最糟糕的是，其中一位合著者在童年的一次潜水事故中受伤，因此他四肢瘫痪，他使用轮椅，而运送他轮椅的流动货车正在接受维修。所以他无法进入他妻子的车，他们必须离开，他必须驾驶他的电动轮椅，穿过掉落的碎片、呼啸的风和烟雾以及所有这些，才能到达一个车辆可以到达的地方，这样他就可以被接走。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. That’s a tough one for the old prediction engine, I got to say. [Laughs.]
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。我不得不说，这对于旧的预测引擎来说是一项艰巨的任务。 [笑。]

paras.en: Szalavitz: No, exactly. And so that was why, like, when I was interviewing them, Laura Harrison brought it up because she was like, “This got put to the test for us very seriously, you know, in these circumstances.”
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：不，完全正确。这就是为什么，当我采访他们时，劳拉·哈里森（Laura Harrison）提出了这个问题，因为她说，“你知道，在这种情况下，这对我们来说是非常严肃的考验。”

paras.en: And so, you know, I wasn’t originally gonna write about any of that. I was just writing about the paper, and so then I had the anecdote that would, like, allow us to get into, you know, the very real-world implications of how we manage uncertainty. And, you know, they were talking about, while they were in that moment, like, thinking about these ideas and thinking about, like, “Okay, well, how do I respond in a proentropic or at least resilient way?” and, you know, “How do I manage the odds of, like, is it safer to stay or go?”
paras.zh: 所以，你知道，我本来不想写这些的。我只是在写这篇论文，然后我就得到了一个轶事，它可以让我们了解我们如何管理不确定性的现实世界的影响。而且，你知道，他们当时正在谈论，就像思考这些想法并思考，“好吧，好吧，我如何以亲熵或至少有弹性的方式做出反应？”而且，你知道，“我如何管理诸如留下或离开更安全之类的可能性？”

paras.en: And so it was really fascinating to think about that. And when you do that, the other thing that becomes very clear is that managing your emotions is very important because your emotions are kind of there, they’re kind of decision-making algorithms to, like, guide you when under uncertainty, right? Like, this has worked in the past, so this will feel good. This doesn’t, so it won’t, right? So you have to be aware of those influences and whether they are guiding you in the right direction or not. And you also have to be aware that, like, when your brain is flooded with stress hormones, you are not thinking about the future the way you ordinarily do because you’re very narrowed in on where you are now, which is important when you’re getting out of a fire.
paras.zh: 所以想到这一点真的很有趣。当你这样做时，另一件事变得非常清楚，管理你的情绪非常重要，因为你的情绪就在那里，它们是一种决策算法，可以在不确定的情况下指导你，对吗？就像，这在过去已经奏效了，所以这会感觉很好。这不会，所以不会，对吧？所以你必须意识到这些影响以及它们是否引导你走向正确的方向。而且你还必须意识到，当你的大脑充满压力荷尔蒙时，你不会像平常那样思考未来，因为你的注意力非常集中在你现在所处的位置，这在你逃离火灾时很重要。

paras.en: But it means that you’re not going to be at your most creative or at your most able to deal with abstraction. And so, you know, this is why, like, in national emergencies, it’s so difficult to manage because we just freak out. [Laughs.] I mean, I sort of feel like what happened, you know, with the pandemic is that that massive social stress moved everybody a notch higher away from planning and abstraction and deeper thought and into a more reactive and often aggressive, unfortunately, mode. So kind of understanding all of this in this context is really useful when you want to try to, like, cope with either on a personal or a, you know, political level the challenges that we are facing now.
paras.zh: 但这意味着你不会发挥出最大的创造力或最有能力处理抽象。所以，你知道，这就是为什么，就像在国家紧急情况下，管理如此困难，因为我们只是吓坏了。 [笑]我的意思是，我觉得，你知道，随着这场大流行病的发生，巨大的社会压力让每个人都远离了计划、抽象和更深入的思考，不幸的是，进入了一种更加反应性、往往更具攻击性的模式。因此，当您想要尝试在个人或政治层面应对我们现在面临的挑战时，在这种情况下理解所有这些确实非常有用。

paras.en: Feltman: Well, and speaking of that shift in the wrong direction that I think we all feel very aware of, you made the point that these phenotypes aren’t really fixed, and that we can change the way our prediction engines work. Could you talk a little bit about how that’s possible?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：嗯，说到错误方向的转变，我认为我们都非常清楚，你指出这些表型并不是真正固定的，我们可以改变预测引擎的工作方式。您能谈谈这怎么可能吗？

paras.en: Szalavitz: So obviously, we are limited, to some extent, by our temperament. Like, I’m never gonna be the chillest person in the world. That probably will not happen. But we can move away from our default responses toward, if they have become dysfunctional, toward more appropriate and, and helpful ones. And you do that by explicitly facing it—not in a way like tough love or force or any of that. And this is a lot of what cognitive-behavioral therapy is. It’s like, you know, “Okay, I walk into the room; I assume they hate me.” That’s my brain doing the assumption. It’s not them doing anything. So I have to be aware of that, and I have to say, “Well, what’s the evidence for my belief that they’re going to hate me?” And there probably isn’t any. And so I need to, like, let go of that and just go into the room with a better expectation. When you face these kinds of things, you have to not assume your perception is automatically correct or real, and you have to assume that it’s provisional.
paras.zh: 萨拉维茨：很明显，我们在某种程度上受到我们的气质的限制。就像，我永远不会成为世界上最冷的人。这可能不会发生。但是，如果我们的默认反应变得功能失调，我们可以摆脱默认反应，转向更合适、更有帮助的反应。你可以通过明确地面对它来做到这一点——而不是以严厉的爱或强制或任何其他方式。这就是认知行为疗法的大部分内容。就像，你知道，“好吧，我走进房间；我认为他们恨我。”这是我的大脑在做这个假设。不是他们在做任何事情。所以我必须意识到这一点，我必须说，“那么，有什么证据可以证明我相信他们会恨我呢？”可能没有。所以我需要放下这些，带着更好的期望走进房间。当你面对这类事情时，你不能假设你的感知自动是正确的或真实的，你必须假设它是暂时的。

paras.en: And the more you can, like, expect surprise and, you know, work toward having the surprises ideally be pleasant ones, then you can get better at managing the whole thing—because it’s kind of amazing how much stuff is, like, building muscle, where it’s just, like, you start with, like, the lower weights, and you suck, and you’re bad at it, and then you repeat it, and then you actually see that you can really get a lot stronger, right? So this is true whether it’s managing stress or, you know, learning anything. But what we tend to do is, sort of, push people into the deep end, and then they’re like, “Well, I can’t do this. I’m bad at this.” It’s like, if you, for your first [time] trying to lift weights, [you] tried to lift 300 pounds, you would not succeed, and you would probably injure yourself, right? But you can, I can attest, build up to this by a lot of practice over many, many years. When it is stress or when it is, like, some of our psychological tendencies, a groove gets worn into your brain because it’s easier and because otherwise we couldn’t possibly handle the complexity of the world.
paras.zh: 你越能期待惊喜，并且，你知道，努力让惊喜最好是令人愉快的，那么你就能更好地管理整个事情——因为令人惊奇的是，有多少东西，比如，锻炼肌肉，就像，你从较低的重量开始，你很糟糕，你不擅长，然后你重复它，然后你实际上发现你真的可以变得更强壮，对吧？所以无论是管理压力还是学习任何东西都是如此。但我们倾向于做的就是，把人们推入深渊，然后他们就会说，“好吧，我做不到。我不擅长这个。”就像，如果你第一次尝试举重，你尝试举起 300 磅，你不会成功，而且你可能会受伤，对吗？但我可以证明，你可以通过多年的大量实践来实现这一目标。当压力或我们的某些心理倾向时，你的大脑就会陷入困境，因为这样更容易，否则我们就无法应对世界的复杂性。

paras.en: So one of the interesting things and implications of the predictive brain stuff is that if you can increase brain plasticity, you can interrupt some of these patterns and help people predict in a more functional way. And it’s really interesting to me that everything, with a few minor exceptions, that has antidepressant effects, whether it’s, like, SSRIs [selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors], exercise, ECT [electroconvulsive therapy], psychedelics, all of these things increase plasticity. And psychedelics do it in an especially interesting way because they seem to open up windows of plasticity that are only open at certain points during development. And so I find that fascinating.
paras.zh: 因此，预测性大脑的有趣之处和意义之一是，如果你可以增加大脑的可塑性，你就可以中断其中一些模式并帮助人们以更实用的方式进行预测。对我来说，真正有趣的是，除了少数例外，所有东西都具有抗抑郁作用，无论是 SSRI（选择性血清素再摄取抑制剂）、运动、ECT（电休克疗法）、迷幻药，所有这些东西都会增加可塑性。致幻剂以一种特别有趣的方式做到这一点，因为它们似乎打开了可塑性之窗，而这些可塑性之窗仅在发育过程中的某些时刻打开。所以我觉得这很有趣。

paras.en: Feltman: Well, thank you so much for coming on to talk to us. Your article was fascinating and it was great talking to you.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：非常感谢您接受我们的采访。你的文章很有趣，和你交谈很愉快。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s all for today’s episode. You can read Maia’s feature online or in the latest issue of Scientific American, which is on newsstands now. We’ll be back on Monday with our weekly science news roundup.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这就是今天这一集的全部内容。您可以在线阅读 Maia 的专题报道，也可以在报摊上最新一期的《科学美国人》中阅读。我们将于周一带着每周科学新闻综述回来。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. Have a great weekend!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。周末愉快！

articles.title: Japan’s MMX mission will reveal the origins of weird Martian moons

paras.en: Roaring away on top of a tongue of flame, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency’s (JAXA’s) ambitious Martian Moons Exploration (MMX) spacecraft launched on its way to Mars on October 19. Its mission: to study the Martian moons Phobos and Deimos, setting down on the surface of the former (along with a small rover) and even returning a 10-gram sample of Phobian material to Earth for later study.
paras.zh: 日本宇宙航空研究开发机构 (JAXA) 雄心勃勃的火星卫星探索 (MMX) 航天器在火焰之上呼啸而过，于 10 月 19 日发射升空，前往火星。它的任务是：研究火星卫星火卫一和火卫二，降落在火卫一的表面（连同一个小型漫游车），甚至将 10 克的火卫一物质样本带回地球供以后研究。

paras.en: The two tiny moons—Phobos is a lumpy space potato that is about 26 kilometers in length, and Deimos is an oddly shaped rock that is about 16 km long—were discovered in 1877 but still hold many mysteries tight. Despite close-up images taken of both by various Mars missions over the decades, there is much we still don’t understand about them, even basics such as how they formed. In fact, this is such a big question that answering it is actually MMX’s primary goal.
paras.zh: 这两颗小卫星——火卫一是一块长约 26 公里的块状太空马铃薯，火卫二是一块形状奇特的岩石，长约 16 公里——于 1877 年被发现，但仍然有许多未解之谜。尽管几十年来各种火星任务拍摄了它们的特写图像，但我们仍然对它们有很多不了解，甚至包括它们如何形成等基础知识。事实上，这是一个很大的问题，回答这个问题实际上是 MMX 的首要目标。

paras.en: I’m excited about this mission! MMX will take a year to voyage to the Red Planet and, once there, will slip into an orbit around Mars that will keep it close to Phobos. It will map Phobos’s surface to measure the moon’s shape and scout for potential landing sites (and will also occasionally observe Deimos from a distance). Once engineers back on Earth choose an appropriate spot on Phobos, MMX will deploy a rover to roam the surface, and soon thereafter, the mission’s main spacecraft will touch down. It will collect a small sample of the surface regolith—the powdery material made from rocks pulverized by meteorite impacts and thermal weathering—and eventually blast off into space once again. The plan is to then fly by Deimos for some close-up observations and to subsequently head back to Earth to return the surface sample in 2031.
paras.zh: 我对这个任务感到很兴奋！ MMX 将花费一年时间航行到这颗红色星球，到达那里后，将滑入围绕火星的轨道，使其靠近火卫一。它将绘制火卫一的表面地图，以测量月球的形状并寻找潜在的着陆点（偶尔也会从远处观察火卫二）。一旦工程师返回地球，在火卫一上选择了合适的地点，MMX 将部署一个漫游车在地表漫游，不久之后，任务的主航天器将着陆。它将收集一小部分表面风化层样本（由陨石撞击和热风化粉碎的岩石制成的粉末状物质），并最终再次飞入太空。计划随后飞越火卫二进行近距离观察，并于 2031 年返回地球返回表面样本。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The rover’s design is pretty clever. It’s a joint effort by France’s National Center for Space Studies (CNES) and the German Aerospace Center (DLR). Called Idefix (after the dog in the French Asterix comic), it has a mass of about 24 kilograms. It’s not much bigger than a large shoebox, although, once the solar panels extend, it will span just more than a meter across.
paras.zh: 火星车的设计非常巧妙。这是法国国家空间研究中心 (CNES) 和德国航空航天中心 (DLR) 的共同努力。它被称为 Idefix（以法国 Asterix 漫画中的狗命名），质量约为 24 公斤。它并不比一个大鞋盒大多少，不过，一旦太阳能电池板延伸，它的跨度将只有一米多。

paras.en: The deployment is pretty gutsy—if successful, it will make Phobos the smallest body ever visited by a wheeled rover. It starts with MMX slowing to a stop about 40 to 100 meters above Phobos and then releasing Idefix.
